licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states
meta.note: Rule rows (PWC25 shape): id, world, statement (paraphrased), locators, speaker, mechanism, seam (AB code), derives (blocked slugs a playable model exists for), default_dial_reason, licence. Proposals: a batched reader (gpt-6-luna) read the books in shards of about 8,000 words; nothing here was human-checked, and no source text is kept.

rules.statement: Faction Beliefs can be compelled against members, but a member may refuse without paying a fate point. They can be invoked only on Factional Skill rolls, never on an individual character’s action.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): FACTIONS — ARE BELIEFS ASPECTS? (fate-srd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limited, group-level beliefs: a setting can widen their influence, at the cost of letting faction doctrine govern more individual actions.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Each Faction assigns its four Skills one rank each: Mediocre (+0), Average (+1), Fair (+2), and Good (+3). Its highest-ranked Belief gets as many stress boxes as its Fealty rating; each other Belief gets one fewer, to a minimum of one.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): FACTION SKILLS (fate-srd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one stress box per Fealty rank for the leading belief, with less for others; a world can increase the boxes to make beliefs harder to change, requiring more conflict.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Each member gains a Status stress track, starting with two boxes; it rises to three when Fellowship is at least Average (+1), and to four when Fellowship is Good (+3) or higher. In faction social conflicts, a character marks Status stress instead of Mental stress; being taken out expels them, while conceding commonly means falling in line.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): FACTION SKILLS / STATUS STRESS (fate-srd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Fellowship setting the track size and faction conflict using Status; a world can make membership more or less resilient, with expulsion or conformity as the social cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A Faction may use Fealty to attack a member’s Status and remove them, with consequences such as punishment or expulsion; Fealty also defends the Faction’s Beliefs when no individual can do so.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): FEALTY (fate-srd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to collective authority policing membership and defending doctrine; a world can soften or intensify this enforcement, at the cost of weaker cohesion or greater repression.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When someone challenges their own Faction’s Beliefs, they roll Provoke against its Fealty in a conflict: the Faction marks Belief stress and the challenger marks Status stress. Winning lets the challenger change the belief; losing brings repercussions.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): BELIEFS IN CONFLICT (fate-srd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a contest that can revise a belief or impose repercussions; a world can make change easier or harder by adjusting Fealty and the stakes of dissent.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In a reasonably public challenge to another character’s Beliefs, both participants may mark stress on their Belief tracks as well as Mental stress. When a Belief track fills, its Faction must reconsider that belief and may instead strengthen it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): BELIEFS IN CONFLICT (fate-srd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to public disputes putting pressure on both belief and mental resilience; a world can make public scrutiny more consequential, risking backlash that hardens doctrine.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A challenge to another Faction’s Beliefs uses Provoke against that Faction’s Fealty. If the challenger forces reevaluation, members who strongly support the belief may seek revenge.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): BELIEFS IN CONFLICT (fate-srd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to outsiders facing the same Fealty resistance plus possible retaliation; a world can reduce or heighten that risk, with disruptive influence inviting revenge.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: At a Significant Milestone, a Faction may swap the ranks of two Skills or add a Belief; at a Major Milestone, it may add one skill point to a Factional Skill or choose a new Paragon.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): IMPROVING FACTIONS (fate-srd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to milestone-based faction advancement; a world can make organizations grow faster or slower, tying improvement to members’ progress.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A result equal to the difficulty is a tie; being one or two above it succeeds, while being three or more above it succeeds with style. Ties move the story forward through a minor cost or partial success; styled success adds a boost when overcoming an obstacle.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Tie; Success; Success with Style (fate-srd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these margin bands; a world can change the thresholds; tighter or looser margins alter how often characters gain clean or enhanced outcomes.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An attack that succeeds deals a hit equal to the difference between attack and defense efforts; the defender must absorb all shifts with stress or consequences or be taken out. On a styled attack, the attacker may reduce the hit by one shift to gain a boost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Attack (fate-srd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to damage by effort difference; a world can change the hit scale; the cost of greater harm is the defender’s limited ability to absorb it.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Aspects describe facts that can grant or remove permission for actions, and can affect difficulty. A boost can be invoked once for free, then disappears; it cannot be compelled or invoked by spending a fate point.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Aspects Are Always True; Boosts (fate-srd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to aspects being binding fictional facts; a world can narrow or broaden their authority; the cost of broad authority is that aspects must fit the fiction.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Creating a new aspect successfully gives one free invoke, or two on a success with style; a tie gives a boost instead. When taking advantage of an existing aspect, success gives one free invoke and styled success gives two, revealing it if it was unknown.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Create an Advantage (fate-srd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one or two free invokes by outcome; a world can change the number or reveal rules; free tactical leverage is the reward for spending an action.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Stress boxes absorb one shift each and clear after the scene. A mild consequence absorbs two shifts, a moderate one four, and a severe one six; consequences remain aspects, and the character who inflicted one gets a free invoke on it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Taking Harm; Stress; Consequences (fate-srd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated capacities and recovery timing; a world can change track size or consequence values; more capacity makes characters harder to remove from a scene.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character can move to an adjacent zone as well as take an action if the route is unobstructed. If movement is impeded, overcoming the obstacle uses the action; an action can instead move the character anywhere on the map, subject to possible difficulty.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Zones (fate-srd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to free adjacent movement when clear; a world can change zone size or movement limits; obstacles cost actions because they make movement risky or interesting.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In a contest, each side makes one overcoming action per exchange, and the highest effort earns a victory; styled success earns two if no other side also styles. The first side to three victories wins, while a tie for highest effort produces a new situation aspect instead of a victory.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Contests (fate-srd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three victories; a world can extend the target, with five recommended as an upper limit; longer contests represent more sustained opposition.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When several characters combine the same skill, the highest-skilled character rolls and each other participant with at least Average (+1) adds +1, up to a bonus equal to the lead character’s skill level. Each supporter spends their action and faces the same costs and consequences as the roller.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Teamwork (fate-srd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated qualification and bonus cap; a world can raise or lower the cap; support costs each participant an action and shares the risk.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character may concede during a conflict only before an opponent rolls. They leave the conflict and lose, choose the terms of their exit, and gain 1 fate point plus 1 for each consequence taken in that conflict; the opposing side must still gain at least part of what it wanted.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Conceding (fate-srd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a negotiated loss before the next opposing roll; a world can increase or reduce the concession reward, reflecting how much leverage the loser earns by paying a meaningful price.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: At a scene’s end, characters clear all stress. Clearing a consequence requires another person to succeed at an overcome action against Fair (+2) for mild, Great (+4) for moderate, or Fantastic (+6) for severe; self-treatment raises the difficulty by 2. After success, the consequence is rewritten as healing, then clears after a full scene, a full session, or a major milestone respectively.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Recovering from Conflicts (fate-srd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed recovery times and treatment difficulties; a world can speed or slow healing, with access to appropriate care explaining the change.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A countdown has a track marked from left to right, triggers that mark boxes, and an outcome that occurs when the last box is marked. Multiple triggers may advance it, and different boxes may have different triggers.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Countdowns (fate-srd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one box per trigger and resolve the stated outcome on the final box; a world can alter track length or trigger frequency to make the looming danger faster or slower.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An extreme consequence reduces incoming stress by 8 and permanently replaces one character aspect other than their high concept. It cannot normally be recovered, may be renamed at the next major milestone, and can be used only once between major milestones.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Extreme Consequences (fate-srd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one irreversible aspect change per milestone interval; a world can loosen recovery or usage limits, with less lasting harm as the trade-off.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A hazard acts once each exchange, using its rating to attack or create advantages, but cannot itself be attacked or overcome. A successful hazard attack adds its Weapon rating, from 1 to 4, to its shifts; attempts to overcome or create advantages against it face passive opposition equal to its rating.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Hazards (fate-srd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a hazard acting each exchange with its listed rating and Weapon value; a world can tune those values to make environmental dangers less frequent or more damaging.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A block imposes passive opposition only when someone tries an action it obstructs; it does not take turns or attack. If it can cause harm, failing to overcome it deals a hit equal to the amount missed, and removing it requires an overcome difficulty equal to its rating plus 2.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Blocks (fate-srd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to situational opposition and a removal difficulty 2 above the block’s rating; a world can make blocks easier to bypass or remove, reflecting the environment’s toughness.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When two opponents differ in scale, the higher-scale side chooses one benefit on any rolled action against the lower: +1 per level before rolling, +2 per level to a successful result, or one additional free invoke per level on a successful advantage creation.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Scale (fate-srd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one chosen benefit per rolled action, measured by scale difference; a world can soften or strengthen the gap to represent how overwhelming supernatural rank is.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A big bad using expendable minion armor can turn a defend-roll failure into success at a cost by making a minion take the hit instead. With reveal true form, taking out one form exposes another, which must be defeated separately with fresh capabilities and tracks; consequences may carry over in reduced form.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ways to Break the Rules for Big Bads (fate-srd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one minion absorbing each redirected hit and at least two sequential forms; a world can limit minions or forms, with fewer defenses and less endurance for the threat.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: For selective attacks on multiple targets, roll once and divide a positive total among them; assign at least 1 shift to each target, and each target defends against its assigned shifts. A zone attack instead makes everyone in one zone, allies included, defend against the full roll; it may require an aspect invoke or stunt.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ways to Handle Multiple Targets (fate-srd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one roll split among targets; a world can permit full-strength attacks on everyone in a zone when the method and circumstances justify the wider danger.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: To affect a whole zone or group with an advantage, put one aspect on the zone or scene rather than on each target. Targets should normally be in the same zone, and one action type should be used unless the GM allows compatible action types in special circumstances.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ways to Handle Multiple Targets (fate-srd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a shared aspect for a group; a world can allow separate target aspects or mixed actions, at the cost of greater bookkeeping or stricter circumstances.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A successful hit gains shifts equal to its weapon rating, including on a tie; on a tie this inflicts stress rather than granting a boost. Armor subtracts its rating from a successful hit, and if the result is 0 or less the attacker gets a boost but causes no harm; ratings are recommended to stay between 0 and 4.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Weapon and Armor Ratings (fate-srd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to weapon bonuses and armor reductions of 0–4 shifts; a world can change that range to make equipment more or less decisive, with greater risk of consequences.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A new skill has two free applications; every additional application costs 1 character point. A skill may be used beyond its usual applications when the GM approves, and an aspect invoke may enable a temporary new action in an unusual case.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Custom Skills — Skill Actions and Applications; Exceeding Recommended Limits (fate-srd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two included applications and a 1-point charge for each extra; a world can loosen application limits, at the cost of setting precedents for other skills.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A mode grants its skills at the mode’s rating; skills can be raised one or two ladder steps above it, but never higher than two. When a skill appears in two modes it starts focused under the higher-rated mode; when present in all three modes it starts specialized there.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Skills Within Modes — Trained, Focused, and Specialized; Reinforced Skills (fate-srd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a two-step skill ceiling and reinforcement from shared modes; a world can alter the ceiling or overlap, changing how concentrated a character’s competence can become.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Characters begin with two mental and two physical stress boxes. A Fair (+2) mode containing a qualifying skill adds one box in that skill’s scope, a Good (+3) mode adds two, and these additions accumulate; a mode with both scopes must choose how to allocate its bonus.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Modes and Stress (fate-srd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two boxes per scope plus mode-based additions; a world can change how many modes grant stress, changing how much harm characters can absorb.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A mega-stunt requires a weird mode and a fitting concept aspect, uses one stunt slot regardless of its number of benefits, and may require a weakness or minor cost. Each benefit beyond the usual stunt-benefit maximum adds one fate point to the GM’s reserve.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Mega-Stunts — What Mega-Stunts Are; Weaknesses and Costs; Paying for Mega-Stunts (fate-srd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permission through concept and mode, with weaknesses or costs for powerful abilities and GM points for excess benefits; a world can adjust those constraints to set the scale of exceptional powers.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An absolute ability automatically succeeds at an appropriate overcome task beyond normal human capability, without a roll; in an opposed roll against someone lacking an equivalent mega-stunt it wins with a success. Every such ability must have a weakness or cost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Mega-Stunts — Absolute Ability (fate-srd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to automatic success only for overcoming and against lesser opponents; a world can narrow the boundary of superhuman capability, with a weakness or cost limiting each ability.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A bulletproof benefit gives Armor:∞ against the specified conventional harm; an attack that ties or succeeds still grants the attacker a boost, while a defense that succeeds with style grants the defender one. It does not prevent attempts to create advantages, and the benefit requires a weakness or cost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Mega-Stunts — Bulletproof (fate-srd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immunity from a defined class of ordinary harm but not advantage-creation; a world can widen or narrow the protected category, with a weakness or cost balancing the immunity.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A voluntary weakness or cost attached to a mega-stunt reduces by 1 the fate points it adds to the GM’s reserve, to a minimum of 0; one benefit cannot have both.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Mega-Stunts (preceding Invention) (fate-srd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to subtracting one reserve point per voluntary drawback; a setting can alter the reduction, trading fewer GM resources for a less attractive benefit.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An invention’s construction check starts at Mediocre (+0) and gains +2 difficulty for each stunt benefit. A failed check still results in the invention being made; its outcome determines the complications required to complete it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Invention — Step Three: Put It Together (fate-srd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to guaranteed completion with difficulty scaled by benefits; a world can make failure block or delay construction, raising the stakes of ambitious designs.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An invention has one catch per stunt benefit. On failure the GM chooses all catches; on a tie the GM and player alternate starting with the GM; on success the GM chooses one and the player the rest; on success with style the player chooses all.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Invention — Step Four: Pay For It (fate-srd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one narrative complication per benefit, with better outcomes granting players more choice; a world can adjust the number or severity of catches to make invention more or less costly.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An invention adds fate points to the GM’s reserve equal to its quality: the number of stunt benefits minus the number of Bugs. A bundled extra containing two or more identical benefits also requires a more severe catch.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Invention — Adding to the GM’s Reserve; Serious Catches (fate-srd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to paying reserve points based on net benefits and intensifying catches for bundles; a world can change these costs to regulate powerful or concentrated inventions.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In a brainstorm, participants roll against Good (+3) to establish facts; a tie earns one victory at a minor cost, success earns one, and success with style earns two. Later fact checks use the previous winning total as their difficulty, or Good (+3) if no one won the earlier check.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Brainstorms — Steps 2–4 (fate-srd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to increasingly difficult fact-finding and victory accumulation; a world can raise or lower the thresholds to make reliable explanations harder or easier to establish.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: At three or more brainstorm victories, a final roll’s winner states a hypothesis that becomes true and replaces the brainstorm’s temporary situation aspects. Three victories give it no free invocation, four or five give one, and six give two; with fewer than three, the GM establishes a mystery aspect instead.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Brainstorms — Step 5: Form a Hypothesis (fate-srd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating a sufficiently supported player hypothesis as fact; a world can require more victories or limit its scope, making narrative truth costlier to establish.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A mission briefing grants one communal fate point to its mission aspect per success on a mission-skill roll, or two per success with style; a tie grants one at a minor cost, and a failure grants none or one at a serious cost. These points can only pay for invoking aspects when using a mission skill and cannot be used for other fate-point expenditures.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Mission Briefings — Step Three: Resource Allocation; The Mission Briefing in Play (fate-srd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a finite, restricted pool supporting anticipated mission skills; a world can change the roll difficulty or permitted uses, balancing preparation against the ordinary fate-point economy.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character begins with one stunt if desired. Refresh starts at 3 and falls by 1 for each stunt beyond the first three, but cannot fall below 1; at session start, a character keeps a larger unspent fate-point total instead of resetting to refresh.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Fate Accelerated — Stunts and Refresh (fate-srd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three free stunts and a minimum refresh of one; a world can set a different free-stunt allowance, trading starting resources for specialization.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Roll four Fate Dice and total their pluses and minuses, or draw from a Fate Deck with the same probability spread. Add the chosen approach and applicable stunt or aspect bonuses, then compare with the opposing total: equal is a tie, greater is success, and being at least 3 higher is success with style.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Dice or Cards; Outcomes (fate-srd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to four dice or an equivalent card draw; the group can choose either randomizer, with no in-world cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Creating or finding an aspect can yield free uses: a tie while making a new aspect gives a one-use boost; success gives one free invocation, and success with style gives two. A failed attempt either produces nothing or lets an opponent invoke the resulting aspect for free; using an aspect already known grants one free use on a tie or success and two on success with style.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Create an Advantage (fate-srd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary aspects with the stated free-use counts; a setting can make advantages rarer by requiring more difficult attempts, because failure may empower an opponent instead.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An overcome action that fails may be abandoned or completed at a serious cost; a tie completes it at a minor cost, success completes it, and success with style also creates a boost. An attack that ties causes no harm but creates a boost; a successful attack deals damage, while success with style can reduce damage by 1 to create a boost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Actions; Overcome; Attack (fate-srd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to costs on failed or tied obstacle-clearing attempts and boosts on ties or stylish outcomes; the GM can make costs harsher or milder to reflect the danger of the situation.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An ally who gives up their action to help adds +1 to the acting character’s roll; the GM decides how many allies can contribute before they impede one another. A character can move one zone for free, but moving at least two zones or passing an obstacle requires an action.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Getting Help; Setting the Scene (fate-srd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a +1 per assisting ally and one free zone of movement; the GM can limit assistance or movement when crowding or obstacles make it costly.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A contest is resolved in exchanges of overcome actions: the highest result wins a victory, success with style counts as two, and a tie gives nobody a victory but introduces a twist. The first participant to collect 3 victories wins.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Contests (fate-srd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a three-victory contest with twists on ties; the GM can change the target or stakes to match the event’s importance.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character begins with 3 stress boxes; a checked box absorbs shifts equal to its number, and only one box can be checked per hit. Mild, moderate, and severe consequences absorb 2, 4, and 6 shifts respectively, but each fills a distinct slot and gives the attacker one free invocation; any unabsorbed hit takes the target out.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ouch! Damage, Stress, and Consequences (fate-srd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three stress boxes and consequence capacities of 2, 4, and 6; a world can make lasting injury more or less common by changing recovery or available absorption, with vulnerability as the cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Stress clears at the end of each scene; mild consequences clear then if the character can rest, moderate consequences generally clear at the end of the next session, and severe ones take longer. A moderate consequence present for two sessions can be cleared at a minor milestone, and a severe one present for at least two sessions can be cleared at a significant milestone.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Getting Better—Recovering from Stress and Consequences; Milestones (fate-srd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated recovery periods; a world can lengthen or shorten them, trading sustained injury for a more or less punishing campaign.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Invoking a known, relevant aspect normally costs 1 fate point and either adds +2, rerolls the dice, raises an opponent’s difficulty by +2, or gives an ally +2. Each aspect can be invoked only once per roll; a free invocation avoids the point cost, and compelling an aspect offers its owner a fate point for accepting the complication, while refusal costs them 1.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Aspects and Fate Points; Invoking Aspects; Compelling Aspects (fate-srd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one paid invocation per aspect per roll and a one-point compel bargain; a setting can alter the fate-point economy, with power and complications balanced by the resource cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A stunt can grant +2 for a specified approach, action, and circumstance; another stunt form allows a special effect once per session. Characters normally begin with 1 stunt, while experienced groups may start with 3 before extra stunts cost refresh; a major milestone can grant 1 refresh point to spend on a stunt.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): How Many Stunts?; Stunts; Major Milestones (fate-srd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to narrow +2 bonuses or one special use per session; a world can allow more stunts by charging refresh, because broader capabilities consume character resources.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: At a significant milestone, raise one approach by 1, but no approach can exceed +5. A major milestone also grants the significant and minor benefits, plus 1 refresh and an optional high-concept rename.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Significant Milestones; Major Milestones (fate-srd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to milestone-based advancement capped at +5; a campaign can award milestones more or less often, controlling how quickly characters grow.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An enemy can be defeated by attacking it and dealing stress; enemies have aspects, skills, and stress, while only some have stunts or consequence slots. Obstacles cannot be attacked and removed that way: PCs must avoid, endure, or otherwise deal with them.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD — Enemies; Obstacles (fate-srd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: enemies can be attacked; obstacles cannot
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making opponents attackable and environmental impediments non-attackable; turn the dial toward more obstacles for tactical or narrative pressure, since they may persist until circumvented or disabled.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A countdown uses a chosen time unit—typically days, hours, minutes, or exchanges—and has a defined consequence when it reaches zero, such as new opposition, death, transformation, or a changed situation.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD — Constraints (fate-srd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a visible clock with a consequence at zero; adjust the unit and consequence to set urgency, with the cost of delay being a changed or worsened situation.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A hazard has a name that functions as both aspect and skill, plus a Weapon rating from 1 to 4. Each exchange it acts using its rating; a successful attack adds its Weapon rating to shifts, and PCs face passive opposition equal to its rating when acting against it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD — Obstacles: Hazards (fate-srd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default hazards to acting each exchange and remaining unattackable; lower the Weapon rating or give a situational way to evade or disable one to reduce persistent danger.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A hazard can be disabled by taking a risk and succeeding at an overcome action against passive opposition equal to its rating. Under suitable circumstances, PCs can instead take a risky extra step to make it attackable as an enemy.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD — Obstacles: Hazards: Using Hazards (fate-srd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring exposure to danger before a hazard can be shut down or made attackable; make the setup safer or harder to change according to how threatening the scene should be.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A block does not take turns; when it interferes with an action, the character rolls against its rating as passive opposition. If a harmful block is not overcome, it deals a hit as though it had attacked and the character had failed to defend by the same margin.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD — Obstacles: Blocks (fate-srd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default blocks to stopping only actions they specifically obstruct; give harmful blocks a Weapon rating when failure should carry physical danger.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When someone forces a target into a block, resolve the attack normally and add Weapon equal to half the block’s Weapon rating, rounded down with a minimum of 1. When a block is used as cover, it either makes an attack impossible or grants Armor equal to half its skill rating, rounded down with a minimum of 1.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD — Obstacles: Blocks (fate-srd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to letting suitable terrain amplify attacks or mitigate incoming ones; decide whether a particular block protects fully or only partially based on what it could plausibly stop.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: To disable a block and remove it from the scene, a character must take a risk and overcome opposition rated two steps above the block. A limitation does not absolutely forbid an action, but acting despite it triggers its stated consequence.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD — Obstacles: Blocks: Using Blocks; Constraints (fate-srd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a risky, difficult action to remove a block and to attaching consequences rather than prohibitions to limitations; increase the pressure through the consequence, not by eliminating player choice.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A distraction poses a choice, may set passive opposition, and has one or more consequences if ignored or handled; resolving it should provide a benefit or avoid a clear consequence.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Distractions; Using Distractions (fate-srd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a clear choice and consequence; turn opposition or the number of repercussions up or down to fit the scene’s pressure and stakes.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A countdown has a track marked from left to right, one or more triggers that mark boxes, and an outcome when the last box is marked. Triggers can be elapsed time or particular events, and different boxes may have different triggers.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Countdowns (fate-srd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one repeated trigger and a stated outcome; vary track length, triggers, or outcome timing to change urgency, with delay allowing the threat to worsen.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A limitation changes how a threat is approached but does not forbid an action. It can be represented by a fact or an aspect; an aspect can be invoked or compelled, and a limitation may have a Weapon rating that inflicts that much stress when its compel is accepted.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Limitations (fate-srd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to discouraging rather than barring an action; turn the consequence dial with a Weapon rating, paid for through accepted compels.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A resistance prevents a specified approach through a lock aspect, which applies without spending fate points; a key—such as an aspect, person, extra, or fictional element—bypasses the lock.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Resistances (fate-srd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one lock and a discoverable key; make the key harder to obtain to create an adventure, at the cost of risking a frustrating roadblock.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A zone can represent physical position or a conceptual state, and a character can occupy more than one zone at once. A mobile zone may move between zones and can share a zone with its occupants.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Types of Zones; Occupying Multiple Zones at Once; Mobile Zones (fate-srd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to zones as flexible fictional positioning; vary how many zones overlap or move to make positioning more or less complex.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A zone’s aspects, obstacles, and constraints can give its environment mechanical effects; for example, activated machinery can become a Great (+4) block with Weapon:2, while snipers can be a Superb (+5) hazard with Weapon:3.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Make Each Zone Count (fate-srd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a few distinctive zones with stated effects; turn the number and severity of hazards to change environmental danger and tactical importance.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: The GM may offer free invokes on environmental aspects: one shared invoke per zone, two per character, or one per character per aspect. Once those free uses are spent, further use requires fate points or advantages.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Offer Free Environmental Invokes (fate-srd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one shared free invoke per zone; give more to encourage environmental interaction, accepting easier fights and greater character power.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A countdown can have multiple triggers and can be attached to a threat or a longer plan; marking its final box causes its outcome, such as reinforcements arriving or a bomb exploding. A failed attempt to disarm the example bomb by 2 or more shifts also marks a box.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Countdowns; Ticking Time Bomb; Forward Scout; Baron von Darkness (fate-srd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to triggers tied to elapsed time or specific events; add event-based stages for a longer plot, with the cost that missed intervention advances the threat.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A Fate game starts with two setting issues, each written as an aspect; anyone may invoke, compel, or create an advantage on these aspects at any time. The group can instead choose one or three issues, changing the focus or number of pressures in play.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Setting’s Big Issues (fate-srd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two broadly available issue aspects; turn the dial to one for a focused story or three for a world with strained resources, reflecting the desired scope.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Aspects can provide a bonus, complicate a character’s life, or add to another character’s roll or passive opposition. When an aspect comes into play, a player or GM will usually spend or gain a fate point.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Defining Aspects; Defining Fate Points (fate-srd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fate points mediating aspect use; a setting can adjust how often aspects affect outcomes, with the cost expressed through its fate-point economy.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Players begin each scenario with fate points equal to their refresh. If a session ends mid-scenario with fewer points than refresh, their pool resets to their refresh; the GM receives a spending budget for each scene.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Defining Fate Points (fate-srd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to refresh-based player replenishment and a scene-based GM budget; change either dial to alter how freely the group can affect events.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character starts with refresh 3 and three free stunts. Taking a fourth or fifth stunt lowers refresh by one per extra stunt, but refresh cannot fall below 1.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stunts and Refresh; Adjusting Refresh (fate-srd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to trading starting fate-point capacity for extra stunts; raise the free-stunt allowance or refresh to make characters more capable with less pressure to accept compels.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Characters normally have two physical and two mental stress boxes, plus one mild, one moderate, and one severe consequence slot. Physique or Will at Average (+1) or Fair (+2) adds one box to its corresponding track; at Good (+3) or higher it adds two, and at Superb (+5) or higher it also adds a harm-specific mild consequence slot.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stress and Consequences (fate-srd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two boxes per stress track and three general consequence slots; add capacity for greater resilience, at the cost of longer conflicts.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In quick character creation, a player may leave most of the character unfinished but must record a high concept, best skill, and name, and begins with 3 refresh. Empty skill slots can be filled when used; an unrecorded skill can instead be rolled at Mediocre (+0).
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Quick Character Creation; Starting Play; Filling Skills in Play (fate-srd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to gradual character definition with unlisted skills at Mediocre; require more choices up front for a more fully specified character.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In quick character creation, three stunts are free and may be written in at any time. Each additional stunt costs a fate point to establish and reduces refresh by one for the next session.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Filling Stunts in Play (fate-srd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three free stunts and charge for later extras through fate points and next-session refresh; change the dial to make spontaneous character development cheaper or rarer.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A relevant aspect can be invoked by spending 1 fate point to gain +2 after a roll, reroll all dice, give another character +2, or add +2 to passive opposition (including creating Fair (+2) opposition). Multiple different aspects can affect one roll, but the same aspect cannot be invoked more than once on that roll.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Invoking Aspects (fate-srd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one paid invocation per distinct aspect for a listed benefit; a world can change which benefits are allowed or their size, at the cost of changing how fate points shape outcomes.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A successful advantage creation gives an aspect one free invocation, or two on success with style; an inflicted consequence also gets one. Free invocations cost no fate points and can stack with paid or other free invocations, including to give +4, two rerolls, or split benefits.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Free Invocations (fate-srd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to granting free uses as described; a world can limit stacking or transfer between characters, trading teamwork potential for simpler bonuses.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When a compel is accepted, the character receives 1 fate point and the agreed complication happens despite attempts to mitigate it. A character can instead pay 1 fate point to prevent the complication; a player proposing a compel against someone else pays 1 fate point, while the GM and a player compelling their own character do not.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Compelling Aspects (fate-srd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated one-point reward, refusal cost, and proposer cost; a world can adjust these amounts or who may compel, at the cost of weakening or intensifying the incentive to accept complications.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Situation aspects are temporary and normally last for a scene, or until they stop making sense, with a session as the maximum. A situation aspect can be removed by an overcome action or another successful action that makes it nonsensical; if no meaningful risk or opposition exists, it can be removed without a roll.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Situation Aspects; Removing or Changing an Aspect (fate-srd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to scene-length aspects and removal when fiction or action warrants it; a world can extend durations or require rolls, at the cost of keeping obstacles in play longer.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Consequences are lasting aspects taken to avoid being taken out; they last from a few scenes to a scenario or two depending on severity. Others may invoke or create an advantage on one when they can justifiably benefit from it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Consequences (fate-srd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to severity-based duration and shared use when justified; a world can make consequences shorter or longer, at the cost of changing how persistent conflict injuries and problems are.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A boost is a highly temporary aspect gained after an insufficient advantage attempt or as an added benefit for especially strong success. Its holder may invoke it for free once, after which it disappears; the holder may let another character use it if relevant.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Boosts (fate-srd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one free use before removal; a world can permit more uses or restrict passing it on, trading fast-changing advantages for more persistent or individual benefits.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character starts a session with 3 fate points by default and may spend up to 2 refresh to buy stunts, but refresh cannot fall below 1. Unspent points above refresh carry into the next session without a new grant, while a new scenario resets the total to refresh.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Fate Point Economy — Refresh (fate-srd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to refresh 3, the stated stunt tradeoff, and scenario reset; a world can change the starting supply or reset timing, at the cost of changing how often characters can invoke aspects.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: At each scene, the GM receives 1 fate point for every PC present to spend for any NPC. The pool resets each scene, with specified carryover when a compel ends or starts a scene or an NPC concedes a conflict; unused extra points can wait for the next scene with significant NPC interaction.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The GM and Fate Points (fate-srd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one NPC point per PC per scene with the stated carryover; a world can alter the pool or carryover, at the cost of changing NPCs’ ability to invoke aspects.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A stunt gives its character a distinctive way to use a skill. Taking a fourth stunt or any later stunt reduces refresh by 1 for each new stunt beyond the first three.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Defining Stunts; Stunts and Refresh (fate-srd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to individual, skill-specific exceptions; a setting can broaden or narrow the options, with each stunt beyond three costing 1 refresh.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A stunt can let a skill perform an action it normally cannot, but only in specified situations; its use is optional. It can instead give a narrow bonus, usually +2 to the skill total or 2 shifts of extra effect, and that added effect can be worth 2 shifts.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Building Stunts; Adding a New Action to a Skill; Adding a Bonus to an Action (fate-srd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to optional, tightly scoped skill modifications; a world can widen the eligible actions or conditions, at the cost of making a stunt less distinctive.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A stunt can make a narrow exception to a game rule, but cannot change the rules for aspects, including invoking, compelling, and the fate point economy.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Building Stunts; Creating a Rules Exception (fate-srd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to narrow exceptions while leaving aspect and fate-point rules fixed; a world can vary which other rules are open to exceptions.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Stunts should be limited by the action they affect, the situations in which they apply, or both; they can also be restricted to once per conflict, scene, or session. A powerful stunt can instead cost a fate point to use, especially if it adds extra conflict harm.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Balancing Stunt Utility; Fate Point-Powered Stunts (fate-srd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to narrow circumstances or a stated use limit; a world can make powerful effects more frequent, but may charge fate points to restrain their impact.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A stunt family has a prerequisite stunt that qualifies a character for related stunts. An upgrade that stacks effects replaces the prerequisite’s effect and costs two stunt slots and two refresh in total.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stunt Families; Stacking Effects (fate-srd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to prerequisite-based families, with stacked upgrades replacing the base stunt; a world can allow more branches or upgrades, spending additional slots and refresh.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Social skill successes can change another character’s emotional state or what they accept as true, but do not dictate actions against that character’s nature. The character’s player chooses the response’s form without canceling the successful advantage.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Social Skills and Other Characters (fate-srd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to successful social effects that grant an advantage without controlling choices; a world can increase how forceful those effects are, at the cost of player agency.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: By default, having a skill that needs tools means the character has the tools needed to use it, and their effectiveness is included in the skill result.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Skills and Gear (fate-srd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating necessary tools as included in the skill; a world can make gear independently important, adding separate access and effectiveness limits.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When ramming another vehicle with Drive, the attacker takes the same number of shifts of harm it inflicts. A stunt may reduce that cost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Drive; Drive Stunts (fate-srd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to equal harm returned by ramming; a world can soften or remove the cost, making vehicle attacks safer.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Empathy can help another character recover from a mental consequence; the listed Psychologist stunt can reduce its severity once per session on a successful roll, with difficulties of +2, +3, or +4 for mild, moderate, or severe consequences, and requires a half-hour conversation.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Empathy; Empathy Stunts (fate-srd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ordinary recovery assistance; a world can permit immediate severity reduction with a limited use, a difficulty based on severity, and time spent treating the subject.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A successful attack inflicts a hit equal to its shifts; the target absorbs it with stress or consequences, and is taken out if unable to do so. On a tie there is no hit and the attacker gets a boost; succeeding by 3 or more also permits a boost if the hit is reduced by 1.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Four Actions — Attack (fate-srd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to hits being absorbed by stress or consequences; a world can make attacks more or less severe by changing what resources absorb them, because targets may otherwise be taken out.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Creating a new aspect yields one free invocation on a success and two on a success with style; a tie gives a boost instead. When using an existing aspect, a tie or success gives one free invocation, while success with style gives two; failure can give the invocation to someone else.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Four Actions — Create an Advantage (fate-srd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to aspects granting limited free uses; a world can change the number of uses or who receives them, because advantage can shift to an opponent on failure.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character who ties an overcome roll achieves the goal at a minor cost; failing may mean failure or success at a serious cost. Success has no cost, and success with style adds a boost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Four Actions — Overcome (fate-srd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to costs increasing as outcomes worsen; a world can require failure rather than costly success, because the GM determines what setback fits.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A defend tie grants the opponent a boost; a successful defense avoids the attack or advantage attempt, and success with style also gives the defender a boost. Failure allows the attempted harm or advantage to take effect.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Four Actions — Defend (fate-srd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to defense blocking the attempted effect on success; a world can grant a defensive counter-benefit on strong results, because turning the tables creates an opening.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In the example skill list, Notice and Will at Average (+1) or Fair (+2) grant a 3-point stress box; Good (+3) or Great (+4) grant 3- and 4-point boxes; Superb (+5) or higher also grant a mild consequence slot. Physique uses the same stress thresholds, but its consequence slot is for physical harm and Will's is for mental harm.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Physique — Special; Will — Special (fate-srd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to skill rank increasing stress capacity and unlocking a harm-specific mild consequence slot; a world can change the thresholds or harm type, because greater fortitude permits more absorption.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A successful Resources roll that is not a success with style can impose a temporary aspect showing depleted wealth; repeated success can worsen it, and it can clear after a spending break or at session end. Alternatively, each successful Resources roll lowers that skill by one rank for the session, and a success at Mediocre (+0) ends further Resources rolls that session.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Resources — Limiting Resources (fate-srd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to wealth use causing temporary depletion; a world can instead lower the skill rank or forbid further rolls, because repeated spending exhausts available resources.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Once per scene, a character can spend a fate point to vanish even in plain sight, gaining a boost; others cannot attack or create advantages on them until they succeed at a Notice overcome roll. The boost ends when invoked or when someone succeeds at that search.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stealth Stunts — Ninja Vanish (fate-srd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a paid, scene-limited disappearance that requires a successful search to counter; a world can alter its cost or duration, because the effect is temporary and can be exposed.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Treat related tasks serving one overall goal as a single overcome action; use separate overcome rolls when tasks create independent tension or require different skills. A challenge consists of one roll per task, and results are interpreted after all rolls are collected.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Challenges (fate-srd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to separate rolls only for independently dramatic tasks; a world can combine them into one roll to streamline play, because the details then shape the cost of failure.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In a contest, participants roll once per exchange, and the highest result wins a victory. A sole success with style earns two victories; a tie earns none and adds a new situation aspect, and the first to three victories wins.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Contests (fate-srd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three victories and a twist on ties; a world can change the victory target or tie outcome to adjust contest length and volatility.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In a conflict, each participant gets one action per exchange, but may defend any number of times. A character can instead forgo their action to gain +2 on all defenses until their next turn.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Exchange / Full Defense (fate-srd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one proactive action and unrestricted defense; a world can alter defense frequency or its bonus to make conflicts more or less tactical.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A hit’s shifts can be absorbed with one stress box of equal or greater value, or with consequences that reduce the hit by 2, 4, or 6 shifts; unabsorbed shifts take the character out. Characters normally have 1- and 2-point boxes in each of two stress tracks, and cleared stress returns after the conflict.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stress / Consequences (fate-srd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these stress boxes and consequence values; a world can change the available buffers to make characters more or less durable, at the cost of changing conflict severity.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A mild, moderate, or severe consequence requires recovery opposition of Fair (+2), Great (+4), or Fantastic (+6), respectively; self-treatment raises difficulty by two ladder steps. After a successful recovery action, wait one scene, one session, or one scenario, respectively, before clearing it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Recovering from a Consequence (fate-srd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to those difficulties and recovery waits; a world can shorten or lengthen them to set how persistent injuries and setbacks are.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An extreme consequence absorbs up to 8 shifts, but requires replacing a non-high-concept aspect and can be used only once between major milestones. It cannot be recovered before the next major milestone.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Extreme Consequences (fate-srd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one costly 8-shift option per milestone interval; a world can change its capacity or frequency, with permanent character change as the price.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A participant may concede before an action’s roll, leaving the conflict and giving the opposing side its goal or removing the conceding character as a concern. The conceder receives one fate point, plus one for each consequence already taken in that conflict.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Conceding the Conflict (fate-srd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concession before dice are rolled and award fate points for it; a world can alter the timing or reward to change how attractive retreat is.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Movement between adjacent zones is free alongside an action if unimpeded. Moving farther, or moving through an obstruction or another character, requires an Athletics overcome roll as the exchange’s action; failure stops movement, a tie permits movement but grants the opponent a temporary advantage, and success with style also grants a boost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Movement (fate-srd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one free adjacent-zone move; a world can make movement costlier or freer to emphasize terrain and positioning.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: To protect someone by physically stepping between them and an attack, defend normally and take the resulting stress and consequences yourself. Protecting them without interposing requires a stunt.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Other Actions in a Conflict (fate-srd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring the defender to interpose and bear the harm; a world can turn on remote protection through stunts, reflecting unusual training or abilities.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An advantage can leave a target Blinded, requiring an overcome action to clear the aspect before they do something that depends on sight, or disarmed until they use an overcome action to recover their weapon.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Other Actions in a Conflict (fate-srd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making these hindrances persist until overcome; a world can vary how readily they can be cleared, based on the circumstances.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: During a challenge in a conflict, a character must successfully defend in any exchange where someone attacks them or creates an advantage against them before they can attempt another challenge goal. If neither happens successfully, they can use their action on a challenge goal.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Other Actions in a Conflict (fate-srd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a successful defense when threatened; a world can relax this for less dangerous challenges, reflecting lower immediate risk.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A conflict ends when everyone on one side has conceded or been taken out. Then award fate points earned through concession and invocations against a character, record consequences, and clear stress-box checks; do not award these yet if the scene shifts into a contest or challenge that still needs resolution.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ending a Conflict; Transitioning to a Contest or Challenge (fate-srd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to settling conflict rewards and clearing stress at the end; a world can defer settlement through a continuing contest or challenge, keeping the unresolved stakes active.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When combining the same skill, the highest-skilled participant leads; each other participant with at least Average (+1) in that skill adds +1, and only the lead rolls. On failure, the group shares the possible costs.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Teamwork (fate-srd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to +1 per eligible helper and shared failure costs; a world can change who qualifies or how costs are shared, reflecting its approach to coordinated effort.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When several characters create advantages to help one person, they can give that person their free invocations; free invocations from the same aspect can stack and be spent together.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Teamwork (fate-srd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing all earned free invocations to stack; a world can limit stacking, making coordinated setup less powerful.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A failed roll can still grant the goal at a cost. A serious cost can include stronger opposition, a new obstacle, delayed success, or a logical consequence; the margin of failure can gauge its severity, with 1–2, 3–5, and 6 or more suggesting increasingly dangerous opposition.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Succeed at a Cost (fate-srd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to matching cost severity to the failure margin; a world can make costs gentler or harsher, reflecting how dangerous failure is.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Extra shifts on a successful action can add an aspect or reduce the time required; for an unopposed advantage attempt in a conflict, or putting an aspect on an object or location, difficulty should not exceed Average (+1) or Fair (+2).
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Setting Difficulties; Dealing with Extraordinary Success (fate-srd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to using extra shifts for added effects or speed and keeping specified unopposed tasks at +1 or +2 maximum; a world can tune difficulty to the narrative stakes.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Story time is the time characters experience, and normally has no fixed relationship to the time spent playing; the GM can summarize elapsed time or make it part of a roll’s result.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Story Time (fate-srd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to treating story time flexibly; turn on explicit tracking when urgency matters, because elapsed time can put goals at risk.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: For a deadline, the GM can track how long actions take, including attempts that fail; challenges and contests already limit how many rolls can happen before an outcome. Success at a cost can grant the desired result but take longer, while exceptional success can shorten the time required.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Deadline Pressure; Using Story Time in Success and Failure (fate-srd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to loose time estimates; track every action when a deadline is pressing, since delays may make the characters arrive too late.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Represent an action’s starting duration as half, one, a few, or several units of time. Each shift changes that duration by one step: for example, from several hours, one, two, or three favorable shifts reduce it to a few hours, one hour, or half an hour; four reduce it to several minutes, while failing by one increases it to half a day.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): How Much Time Is a Shift Worth? (fate-srd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to approximate time categories and one-step changes per shift; use more granular durations if desired, with the cost of extra tracking.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A roll can cover an extended period and affect broad events, not just an immediate person-to-person action. When a conflict spans a long period, scale each exchange to match it; one exchange might represent a month or two in a year-long conflict.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Story Time and the Scope of an Action (fate-srd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rolls covering the immediate action; widen their scope for long breaks or large goals, accepting that one roll can reshape the setting.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: To attack several specific targets, divide the rolled total among them; each target defends separately, and a target who fails takes stress or an aspect as appropriate. An advantage that gives aspects to several targets grants one free invocation for each target. An attack on a whole zone or scene instead calls for each person there to defend against the roll.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Affecting Multiple Targets (fate-srd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to target-by-target defenses and divided totals; allow whole-zone effects when the fiction supports them, since they can expose everyone in the area.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A compel intended to affect multiple targets costs one fate point per target, even if one or several aspects justify it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Compels and Multiple Targets (fate-srd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to charging separately for each compelled individual; a setting can vary that price, with broader influence otherwise becoming unusually cheap.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A hazard without self-awareness can be treated as a character: give it skills to attack, create aspects, or sense aspects, and let characters use skills against it. A sufficiently difficult hazard can have stress and consequences; something too large to overcome may instead call for avoidance or escape as a challenge.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Environmental Hazards (fate-srd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to modeling hazards with character-like actions; simplify minor threats or make dangerous ones more elaborate, at the cost of additional tracking.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A mob of identical nameless NPCs acts as one unit and rolls once; when hit, shifts beyond those needed to take out one member carry over to the next members individually. Helpers add to the mob’s effectiveness, and a reduced mob’s remaining member can join another group or flee.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Mobs; Hits and Overflow (fate-srd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to grouping identical minor opponents and carrying excess hits forward; split them into individuals when their separate actions matter, with more bookkeeping.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Supporting NPCs have a high concept, trouble, at least one more aspect, one stunt, two stress tracks with two boxes each, roughly four or five skills, and one mild consequence; a tougher one may also have one moderate consequence. Add any stress boxes granted by a skill.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Supporting NPCs (fate-srd#015)
