rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default supporting NPCs to this compact sheet; the GM can turn toughness up with a moderate consequence or extra skill-based stress capacity to keep a recurring opponent in play.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A supporting NPC may have a peak skill one or two levels above the best PC only when serving as serious opposition; allied supporting NPCs should be near the PCs’ skill level. A Great peak uses a descending column with one Good, one Fair, and one Average skill beneath it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Supporting NPCs — Skill Levels (fate-srd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to peers for allies and a one- or two-level edge for serious opposition; turn the dial higher only to make a lieutenant a notable threat.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Supporting NPCs should concede conflicts when they can, particularly early in a story; a concession awards one or more fate points and can make the NPC more dangerous on a later appearance. Main NPCs, by contrast, may fight to the bitter end.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Supporting NPCs — Concessions; Main NPCs (fate-srd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default supporting characters to conceding rather than fighting until defeat; the GM can reserve relentless opposition for main NPCs, while concessions award fate points and set up later encounters.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A main NPC can match the PCs’ current skill distribution or remain a static superior; in the latter case, give them enough skills to reach at least two levels above the game’s current skill cap. For a Great (+4) cap, that means supporting a peak of Fantastic (+6).
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Main NPCs (fate-srd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default a major antagonist to a PC-matching or static-superior skill profile; turn the dial toward a two-level advantage for a lasting villain, whose high competence creates sustained opposition.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When several characters oppose the PCs, avoid outnumbering them unless the opponents have lower comparative skills. For one major opponent facing the group, set that opponent’s peak skill two levels above the best relevant PC skill; usually keep to one main NPC per scene except for an arc finale.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Playing the Opposition — Right-sizing (fate-srd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to modest numbers and one main opponent; increase enemy count or peak skill for a climactic challenge, at the cost of a harder conflict.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: NPCs can create advantages to gather information and build free invocations rather than directly blocking the PCs. On their home turf, NPCs may start with free invocations on situation aspects they had time to establish; two or three such aspects is already near the suggested limit.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Playing the Opposition — Creating Advantages for NPCs (fate-srd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default NPCs to using advantages as well as direct opposition; the GM may preload two or three justified home-turf aspects with free invocations, reflecting preparation.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A scenario usually lasts one to four sessions and contains several scenes; resolving or making its central problem unresolvable ends it, and its end should trigger a significant milestone. One or two core problems are sufficient, while one to three story questions typically fit a session, four to eight may take two or three sessions, and more than eight or nine may need another scenario.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Defining Scenarios; How Many Problems Do I Need?; Ask Story Questions (fate-srd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-to-four-session scenario with one or two problems; turn its length by adding story questions, with a significant milestone as the reward for resolving the problem.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A scene should have a clear purpose and begin just before an interesting event; it ends once the PCs achieve or fail at that goal, or can no longer achieve it. The GM may cut to a new scene when momentum flags.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Defining Scenes — Starting Scenes (fate-srd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default scenes to one goal and an event-ready opening; the GM can cut sooner when momentum fades, trading exhaustive moment-to-moment play for brisk pacing.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A GM may present opening trouble as pre-loaded compels and award fate points at the start of a session. This can give low-refresh players resources to spend, but should be used only when the group accepts the GM narrating them into trouble.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Set Up the First Scene — Powerful Session-Starting Ninja GM Trick (fate-srd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to player agreement before imposing opening trouble; turn the dial toward pre-loaded compels to grant fate points and launch action, at the cost of some player control.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A minor milestone lets a character make exactly one of these changes: swap two skill ranks, replace an Average (+1) skill, change or buy a stunt (a purchase requires enough refresh and cannot reduce refresh below 1), or rename a non-high-concept aspect. The character may also rename moderate consequences to begin recovery.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Minor Milestones (fate-srd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one modest, story-justified sheet change; a world can allow more changes for faster adaptation, at the cost of looser continuity.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A significant milestone gives the benefits of a minor milestone, plus one skill point to buy a skill at Average (+1) or raise a skill one rank; it also allows renaming severe consequences to begin recovery. Skill ranks must obey the column limit: there cannot be more skills at a rank than at the rank below it, so points may need to be saved or spent first on supporting skills.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Significant Milestones; Skill Columns (fate-srd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one skill point with rank support enforced; a world can waive or defer the column restriction for quicker advancement, at the cost of the intended limit on broad competence.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A major milestone grants minor and significant milestone benefits, and additionally lets a character rename an extreme consequence to move past its worst effects, gain one refresh, exceed the current skill cap if able (raising that cap), and rename their high concept.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Major Milestones (fate-srd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these extra advances only at major campaign turning points; a world can grant them more often for faster power growth, at the cost of needing stronger opposition.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An extra is part of a character’s sheet and is controlled by whoever controls that character; having one requires a permission or a cost. The group decides what extras are appropriate, what they do, what character elements express them, and their costs or permissions.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Defining Extras; Creating an Extra (fate-srd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring an agreed permission or cost and giving control to the character’s controller; a world can make access easier or harder, justified by how common or restricted its special capabilities are.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: The game may model any part of the world as a character, giving it aspects, skills, stunts, stress tracks, and consequences when useful; environmental hazards can therefore act using skills.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Bronze Rule, aka the Fate Fractal (fate-srd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to modeling only elements that need character-like rules; a world can apply this broadly for detailed environments, at the cost of extra rules and attention.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A proposed extra may let its user interact with the supernatural in ways ordinary skills cannot, and may affect or harm people; its basic effects use the ordinary four actions, while rituals are resolved as challenges, contests, or conflicts as appropriate. The group intends these capabilities to be no more powerful than comparable trained skills.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): What Extras Do (Zird’s magic example) (fate-srd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ordinary actions and comparable skill power; a world can make supernatural effects stronger or broader, with the cost of shifting the game’s balance and focus.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An extra can require a character aspect as permission and can be paid for with character-sheet resources such as skill ranks, refresh, stunt slots, or aspect slots. A group may add equal starting slots for every character instead of making extras compete with ordinary options.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Permissions and Costs (fate-srd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to aspect-based permission and ordinary character resources; a setting can waive permission or add equal slots, trading scarcity for broader access.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A successful hit gains shifts equal to its Weapon rating, including on a tie; Armor subtracts its rating from a hit’s shifts. If Armor reduces the result to zero or less, the target takes no harm and the attacker gets a boost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Weapon and Armor Ratings (fate-srd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Weapon adding and Armor subtracting shifts; a world can raise ratings or make strong armor scarce, making equipment disparity consequential.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A power can be built as a stunt; for effects beyond ordinary stunt limits, charge one additional refresh per two shifts, added actions, or rule exceptions. Variable refresh spending can represent stronger levels of a power.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Superpowers (fate-srd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to modest stunt-scale powers; a setting can raise power by charging refresh, so exceptional abilities consume character capacity.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A skill-based magic extra can add magical uses to a skill: Lore can perform rituals or answer arcane questions, alter the environment or impede a target, attack, and defend against magic. Targets can defend against magical mental or physical impediments with Will, and against attacks with Athletics, Will, or magical Lore as appropriate.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Extra: Collegia Arcana Magic (fate-srd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to trained users applying the listed skill actions; a setting can vary permissions, resource costs, and available effects to make magic rarer or more idiosyncratic.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An extra that can be harmed or exhausted may receive its own stress track; a skill can increase that track’s stress boxes or consequence slots. Wealth can likewise be tracked as a stress track, attacked and defended against, with being taken out causing a lasting financial setback.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Assigning Character Elements; Wealth (fate-srd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to tracks only for extras or resources that can be depleted; a world can track more resources this way, increasing the consequences of conflict.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An ancestral power is accessed by spending a free invoke earned with Commune or two fate points. Commune can also add stress and consequence capacity to a karmic track; failed or undefended supernatural actions can cause karmic harm.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Extra: Lucas’s Arts (fate-srd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spirit benefits paid for with invokes or two fate points; a setting can change the price or the spirit relationship, tying power to bargains or spiritual risk.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A spirit of warding can avert one mundane calamity per scene without a roll, but cannot undo an action; it can also create a Great (+4) shield for the user and named allies. The shield ends when opposition gets past it and must then be established again.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Sujan, the Spirit of Warding (fate-srd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one automatic prevention per scene and a +4 shield that ends when breached; a world can alter the frequency or strength, limiting how often fate or force can be denied.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Members of an arcane order use the lower of their order’s skill rank and their Lore rank for magical actions, and can belong to only one order at a time. They receive one of that order’s stunts free and may buy more with refresh.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Schools of Power (fate-srd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the lower skill rank and one order; a setting can loosen membership or skill limits, at the cost of weaker distinctions between magical traditions.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character may choose a heroic sacrifice only before being taken out and before the dice are rolled for the current action. The character dies irrevocably, and the player may also take out nameless NPCs or a supporting NPC, inflict a severe consequence on a named NPC (or escalate an existing severe consequence to extreme), end a conflict by group agreement, or overcome one obstacle without a roll if the group agrees it makes sense.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Chapter 2, Making Player Character Death Count—Heroic Sacrifice (fate-srd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a voluntary, irreversible death that buys one listed benefit; a world can restrict the benefits or require group agreement more often to make sacrifice rarer and costlier.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: After a character dies, the remaining PCs may create one group legacy aspect for that player’s lost character. If the dead character’s player has not made a new character, they receive two free invokes on that aspect each session to help the living PCs.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Chapter 2, Making Player Character Death Count—Legacy Aspects (fate-srd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one legacy aspect per player and two helping invokes per session while they lack a new character; a world can remove the invokes or limit legacies to make death leave less ongoing aid.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A ghost uses Fate Core supporting-NPC rules, keeps the default stress boxes, cannot gain more through Physique or Will, and has one mild consequence slot. If taken out, it must depart the living world; it is ordinarily intangible and cannot be attacked, though it can communicate with living associates. Complicated or stressful messages face Fair (+2) opposition.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Chapter 2, Making Player Character Death Count—Haunting (fate-srd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an intangible, fragile observer with limited communication; a world can allow greater manifestation, but crossing into material action requires creating a Manifested aspect.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: To make a ghost’s effect on the material world more forceful or lasting, it creates a Manifested aspect using Will or another fitting skill. While that aspect lasts, it can directly affect the physical world against the applicable opposition at +2.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Chapter 2, Making Player Character Death Count—Haunting (fate-srd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a created aspect and granting +2 while it lasts; a world can make manifestation harder or shorter-lived to emphasize the cost of crossing between worlds.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: The communal fate-point pool can be spent by any player only on behalf of another PC or an allied NPC, and the acting character must be directly involved. The pool resets to zero at each significant milestone and is capped at the number of players.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Chapter 2, Using a Communal Fate Point Pool (fate-srd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a shared pool capped by group size and reset at milestones; a world can make it supplemental or the sole source of fate points to tune how necessary teamwork is.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When a player self-compels a character flaw, they gain the usual fate point and add one to the communal pool; if that pool is full, they instead gain a free invoke on a setting or situation aspect. If the complication affects the whole group, add two pool points instead.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Chapter 2, Enhanced Self-Compels (fate-srd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rewarding a flaw-driven complication with one shared point, or two for a group complication; a world can reduce the reward to discourage complications or increase it to invite them.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Once per scene, a player who declares an appropriate, directly relevant story detail that is inconvenient or neutral in the current circumstances adds a fate point to the communal pool instead of paying one.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Chapter 2, Encouraging Players to Declare Story Details (fate-srd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one qualifying declaration per scene and a shared point as its reward; a world can narrow what qualifies to limit player-authored complications.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: During reconstruction of a horrific incident, provide at least one clue per group member and let each player elaborate on a clue. For each detail added that complicates the group’s situation, add one point to the communal fate pool.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Chapter 2, Flashbacks & Reconstruction (fate-srd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one clue per player and a shared point for each complicating addition; a world can omit the reward to make reconstruction less likely to introduce new trouble.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: At a minor milestone, a character with an intense emotional bond can replace an aspect with one representing that engagement; an intensity rating runs from +1 to +3 for attraction or -1 to -3 for repulsion. For actions consistent with the rating’s direction, the character may use its absolute value instead of a skill or add +1 to a skill; acting against that direction faces opposition of at least that absolute value, or +1 opposition if the existing opposition is already higher.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): During the Game: Intensity Aspects (fate-srd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ratings from -3 to +3 that affect actions in both directions; a world can narrow the range or weaken the bonuses to make attachments less mechanically dominant; the in-world cost is that intense desire or repulsion complicates choices.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: At a milestone, a character may move an intensity rating one step; reducing it to 0 allows immediate replacement of the aspect. Once per scenario, its object may initiate a contest to change it, and on a win may shift it one step or invert its sign.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Changing Intensity Aspects (fate-srd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one object-initiated contest per scenario and a one-step change or inversion on a win; a world can make such contests more or less frequent; the in-world cause is the object playing on the character’s hopes and fears.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A climactic dilemma is used at most once per scenario. Give each involved player a fate point when it is initiated; if the group chooses an undeclared option, raise opposition by three or four points and make being taken out carry at least an extreme consequence.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Climactic Dilemmas — Resolution (fate-srd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one dilemma per scenario, a fate point for each involved player, and a 3–4 point opposition increase for an unlisted plan; a world can change the reward or penalty; the cost is taking harder odds and potentially severe harm to pursue another path.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A trauma aspect can be invoked or compelled when its triggers fit, and lasts until treated through therapy or a heart-to-heart conversation. While a coping condition is checked, the character also has a trauma aspect with the same name; an opponent who caused it to be checked gets a free invoke.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Trauma Aspects; Coping Conditions (fate-srd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistent trauma aspects and a matching aspect while a coping condition is checked; a world can make treatment easier or harder; the ongoing cost is that triggers can complicate the character’s life.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character taking physical or mental stress may check one coping condition in addition to marking one stress box and any number of consequences. Fleeting, sticky, and lasting conditions absorb 2, 4, and 6 shifts respectively; each character can have only one of each kind.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Coping Conditions (fate-srd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three condition slots absorbing 2, 4, and 6 shifts; a world can change the capacities or slot limits; the cost is taking on maladaptive behavior and a related trauma aspect.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Fleeting coping conditions clear when the scene ends or the character escapes; sticky ones clear through natural recuperation, while lasting ones require help and someone to overcome at least Great (+4) opposition. An unchecked condition can be removed at a minor milestone instead of changing an aspect, and a condition may be upgraded to a more severe free slot.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Coping Conditions (fate-srd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to scene-end, recuperation, and Great (+4) help as the clearing thresholds; a world can make recovery require more or less effort; the cost is time, support, or a difficult success.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A scene’s Gore rating attacks every exchange, defended by Will or Careful; the GM can target one character, divide shifts among several, or attack everyone with the full roll. The GM has a per-scene fate-point reserve to boost these attacks.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Mental Toll of Gore (fate-srd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to repeated scene attacks against Will or Careful with a per-scene boost reserve; a world can vary targets and shift distribution; the cost is stress or consequences incurred while investigating.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A triggered monster stunt can create an advantage representing revulsion or make a Provoke attack against all witnesses. Such a stunt should be limited to once per scene, require a fate point, or require an invoke of a suitable situation aspect.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Splatter Attacks (fate-srd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single scene-limited effect or a fate-point/aspect cost; a world can loosen or tighten those limits; the in-world impact is that witnesses are disturbed by the monster’s appearance or actions.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: While Disturbingly Callous is checked, its bearer is immune to mental attacks based on gore and cannot have visceral aspects compelled against them, but cannot use or defend with Empathy. Clearing it requires a demonstrated act of vulnerability or humanity. Anyone else in the same zone adds 1 shift to each gore attack they receive.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Inured; The Horror of Viscera and Gore (fate-srd#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a checked condition that grants gore resistance but shuts off Empathy; a world can change the protection or the blocked skill, with vulnerability as the clearing cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A fleeting condition represents a temporary resource drain and refreshes each scene; a checked condition can prevent reuse until then. A lasting condition can lock out an ability until cleared, potentially requiring a Great (+4) Physique roll and a full session of waiting. Conditions used to describe a monster’s state do not also absorb conflict stress.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Choose Unique Conditions (fate-srd#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fleeting, sticky, and lasting conditions with the described refresh or recovery limits; a world can alter the duration or recovery test, at the cost of condition capacity or downtime.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Dominate requires a chosen trigger such as eye contact, prior feeding, or tasting the monster’s blood. The monster creates an advantage opposed by Will; it can then mark Domination boxes instead of spending fate points to compel or invoke the resulting enthrallment, and must rest, feed, or otherwise act suitably to clear those boxes.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Example Stunts — Dominate (fate-srd#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a trigger-gated Will contest and limited domination boxes; a world can broaden triggers or remote reach, with recovery actions limiting repeated control.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: On a successful feeding attack, a monster may either start recovering a consequence no worse than the victim’s, or gain a free invoke on its high concept. If the attack inflicted a consequence, the recovering consequence must be of equal or lower severity.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Example Stunts — Drain; Vampire: Suggested Stunts (fate-srd#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to choosing between healing and a temporary power benefit; a world can restrict feeding targets or recovery, with access to victims as the cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When taken out, an indestructible monster cannot be killed unless its extreme consequence is already filled or the final attack invokes its vulnerability. Otherwise it withdraws or seems dead for at least a scene; each participant gains a fate point, and on return the monster clears stress and recovers mild through severe consequences except those caused by vulnerability attacks.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Example Stunts — Indestructible (fate-srd#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary defeat unless the specified kill condition is met; a world can make vulnerabilities more or less decisive, with a delayed return and restored defenses as the cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A spirit can possess a victim indefinitely after taking them out in a mental or physical conflict. It uses the victim’s physical skills and its own mental skills; allies must discover the proper exorcism and defeat it in a conflict. For a PC, the player may spend a fate point to regain limited control for a scene.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Example Stunts — Possess (fate-srd#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to possession after a decisive defeat and an exorcism conflict; a world can make release easier or harder, with research and the victim’s fate point as costs.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Re-Zone can combine up to three zones, split one zone into two or three, swap adjacent zones, or connect two nonadjacent zones. Its first use in a scene is free; each later use costs a fate point.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Example Stunts — Re-Zone (fate-srd#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed bounded zone edits and charge after the first use; a world can widen the edits or alter the price, with fate points limiting repeated spatial changes.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Transform uses sticky conditions to represent alternate forms, which can change skills, abilities, vulnerabilities, or stunt access. Use is free by default, but can instead cost a fate point or be limited to once per scene.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Example Stunts — Transform (fate-srd#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to freely switching among condition-defined forms; a world can impose a scene limit or fate-point cost, making transformation a scarce resource.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A lasting transformation condition cannot be cured without extraordinary circumstances; marking one gives the character an aspect and a free invoke. If the character must mark one but cannot, they transform fully, replace their high concept, and fold all transformation conditions into it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Survivable Alterations (fate-srd#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to accumulating lasting transformation conditions until capacity is exceeded; a world can change the number of stages or cure requirements, with permanent bodily change as the consequence.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: For each scale level an acting character has over an adversary, add +1 to the roll; on a successful roll, add +2 shifts, or on a create-advantage roll, gain one extra free invoke. The scale ladder has five levels, from Mundane to Godlike.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Giving the Other Scale (fate-srd#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one of these benefits per scale step; tune the scale gap or benefit for the desired disparity, because the Other’s resources can overwhelm the characters.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: To transform a character, the Other must first create circumstances that permit the attempt, then inflict a consequence in a conflict. It can attach an agenda-serving, sticky checked condition to one moderate, severe, or extreme consequence; the condition’s effect is roughly as strong as a stunt and ends when that consequence clears.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Transformation (fate-srd#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one checked condition per qualifying consequence after the required setup; tune the condition’s effect and preparation, because transformation requires both access and harm.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: After inflicting an extreme consequence through transformation, the Other can make the character a willing pawn the next time it takes them out. The character becomes a main NPC, recovers all consequence slots, and has their existing transformation conditions permanently checked.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Endgame (fate-srd#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to pawn conversion only after an extreme transformation consequence and a later takedown; change the trigger if the story should make conversion easier or harder.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Once per conflict, liberators can inflict a consequence on a pawn and clear one checked transformation condition. When all such conditions are clear, the pawn is freed; a rescued character may spend a later milestone on recovering memories and gaining a stunt usable against the Other.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Endgame (fate-srd#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one condition cleared per conflict and a milestone cost for recovered memories; adjust the pace to make liberation more arduous or more achievable.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Each doom-clock tick moves time one hour closer to midnight. By default, the clock can be moved back only once per scene; when it runs out, the doom arrives and the game enters its final scene or scenes.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Doom Clock (fate-srd#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one backward tick per scene and an endgame at midnight; permit fewer or more retreats to make doom more certain or more escapable.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character fails with style when their result is at least 2 shifts below opposition, or when they choose that outcome on a failure; their opponent succeeds with style, and the character cannot instead succeed at a cost. At the next scene they receive one token to gain a free invoke, remove a free invoke, or—once per session—move the doom clock back one hour; a player can hold only one token.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Fifth Outcome: Failure With Style (fate-srd#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated 2-shift threshold and one held token; remove the success-with-style option or change token benefits to emphasize desperate sacrifice.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Whenever a character recovers from a moderate, severe, or extreme consequence, or from a sticky or lasting condition, record a scar under their Book of Scars aspect. Each character can record five scars; once all five are used, they can never clear those consequence slots or recover from those conditions, although treatment can rename a consequence without clearing it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Book of Scars (fate-srd#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to five permanent scar entries that eventually prevent recovery; change the capacity to control how quickly injuries become lasting.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Each survivor must periodically spend one free invoke on every necessity; the interval depends on the story’s pace. A survivor unable to pay must lower Physique (or Forceful) by 1, to no lower than Terrible (−2), or take a consequence; if neither is possible, they are taken out.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Not Enough Resources to Go Around: Consumables / Going Without (fate-srd#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one invoke per survivor per necessity at a pace-appropriate interval; shorten the interval to intensify scarcity, with skill loss, consequences, or removal from play as the cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Two survivors on half-rations share one free invoke on the necessity, but each gains a negative situation aspect. When called on to pay a necessity, a survivor may spend one additional free invoke to restore a lost skill point, or, if the skill is already normal, to start recovering a consequence caused by deprivation; only one extra invoke can be used this way.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Consumables Rules Summary / Half-Rations / Recovering from Lack of Necessities (fate-srd#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two survivors sharing a ration invoke and each taking an aspect; allow one extra invoke for recovery, with privation and resource depletion as the cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Players can create an advantage to add free invokes to a consumable when they justify it. A scavenging contest needs three victories to succeed; on success, the group gains two free invokes on suitable consumables per victory, while failure yields none. Each shift the threat scores against NPCs sent scavenging kills a nameless NPC or gives a supporting or main NPC a consequence; survivors returning from the mission bring one invoke per NPC sent.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Gaining Free Invokes on Consumables / Sending NPCs to Scavenge (fate-srd#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to justified resource gains from scavenging or trade; raise opposition as nearby supplies are depleted, and make NPC missions risk casualties or consequences.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A PC without stress must absorb a hit with a consequence or sacrifice an NPC survivor. The NPC’s permitted harm depends on their status and relationship: for example, a nameless NPC can be severely maimed to avoid a mild consequence or die to avoid a moderate one; a main NPC with a significant positive relationship can take a consequence one severity lower, or die or become a permanent enemy to avert an extreme consequence.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Whittling Down the Survivors / NPC Survivor Consequence Summary (fate-srd#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to redirecting PC harm to eligible NPCs according to significance and relationship; make the cost maiming, death, or lasting enmity among the survivors.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When a supporting NPC dies, promote a nameless NPC to supporting status at the next minor milestone. When a main NPC dies or becomes a permanent enemy, promote a supporting NPC to main status and a nameless NPC to supporting status at that milestone.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Supporting NPCs / Main NPCs (fate-srd#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to replacing lost survivor roles at the next minor milestone; turn the remaining group into a continuing cast while preserving the loss.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A haven has no stress and has mild, moderate, and severe consequence slots; being taken out means it is destroyed or overrun and the group must flee. In an abstract attack, a failed defense deals a hit equal to the attacker’s shifts, uses haven consequences or NPC sacrifices to absorb it, and breaches the perimeter; an unrepaired haven consequence can instead serve as an attacker’s point of ingress.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Managing “Safe” Havens / Designing a Safe Haven / Attacks on a Haven (fate-srd#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three haven consequence slots and breach after a failed defense; adjust attacker strength or repair access to tune safety, with destruction or flight as the endpoint.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Haven consequences cannot be fully repaired: an overcome action can change one into a less harmful defensive condition, but the haven continues to deteriorate and may eventually fall. If a horror aspect is inflicted on a character, the GM chooses when it is assigned rather than letting the player create it; self-compelling that aspect earns a horror point instead of a fate point, and horror points are worth double a fate point’s usual benefit (+4, or a reroll and +2).
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Attacks on a Haven / Feminine Horror Aspects and Horror Points (fate-srd#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to incomplete haven repairs and GM-timed horror aspects; turn the deterioration or loss of agency dial upward, rewarding self-compels with stronger but themed points.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character with the aspect Doubt Your Own Senses can invoke or be compelled in ways that let a player or GM rewrite an event already established in play. Lost and Found can be invoked or compelled to make useful items appear or be removed at consequential moments.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Insidious Gaslighting (fate-srd#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing aspect-based reinterpretation or item disappearance; make the effect personal or setting-wide, with uncertainty and lost resources as the cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A successful attack checks off one relevant condition; a success with style checks off two. A character may also check off a condition to succeed at a cost, and is taken out if required to mark one but has no relevant condition available.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Spooky Fun — Conditions (fate-srd#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one marked condition per successful attack and two for success with style; a world can make attacks harsher or gentler by changing how many conditions they require, reflecting its level of danger.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A marked condition also gives the character an aspect of that name with one free invoke available to enemies. Conditions remain marked until a specific event clears them; some may require overcoming passive opposition of at least Fair (+2).
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Spooky Fun — Conditions / Removing Conditions (fate-srd#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sticky conditions that create an enemy advantage until cleared; a world can make recovery easier or harder, reflecting how lasting its troubles are.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Courage is a shared score for the current menace, starts at zero for each new menace, persists between sessions, and cannot exceed that menace’s Fear rating. The group gains one point for understanding a clue about the menace’s motive or weakness, self-sacrificing to help another, or proposing a twist.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Never Say Die — Courage (fate-srd#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a shared, capped Courage pool that grows through discovery, teamwork, and twists; a world can change its cap or how it is earned, reflecting how knowledge and solidarity help overcome fear.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When each character separately faces a menace or its minion, they roll to overcome with Courage. The group’s Courage applies only when everyone is together and nobody has been taken out; otherwise an isolated character uses Mediocre (+0). If everyone fails or ties, all flee and take a related condition; if anyone succeeds, the group may stay, but those who fail or tie must still pay a cost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Never Say Die — Overcoming Fear (fate-srd#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Courage helping only a united, active group; a world can loosen that requirement or make separation more costly, reflecting how much the heroes rely on one another.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A menace has a Fear skill and conditions suited to its nature; as a starting point, give it a number of conditions equal to half its Fear. Its marked conditions typically cannot be cleared, and if it must mark one but has no relevant condition left, it is taken out for good.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Menace — Fear / Weaknesses / Taken Out (fate-srd#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent damage against a menace and a condition capacity based on half its Fear; a world can give it more or fewer conditions, reflecting how difficult it is to defeat.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character taken out is unable to act, but the result should fit the genre rather than cause injury or death; examples include being overcome by fear, confined, or having something important taken away. When a character is taken out, the remaining group’s Courage is treated as Mediocre (+0).
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Never Say Die — Being Taken Out / Overcoming Fear (fate-srd#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to nonlethal, temporary removal from action and a weakened Courage pool; a world can make the setback more or less severe, reflecting its intended horror tone.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: While a character has the Host consequence, it may be compelled to take risks to investigate the parasite or protect others. A fate point can pass the Host consequence and Maternal Instinct stunt to another player, or give that player the Fatalist mild consequence instead.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Alien Pregnancy — Example Setup (fate-srd#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing a fate-point payment to shift the parasite-related burden; a world can prohibit or alter transfer, reflecting whether the infestation can spread between hosts.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Coach Wimbly must consume batteries daily to survive; without them he fades away. Keeping him from his supply weakens him, while a device that draws power from him or a computer virus could shut him down.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Hotspot — Weaknesses (fate-srd#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to daily battery consumption as a survival requirement and power-draining or hacking as countermeasures; a world can change the deadline or the effectiveness of these methods, reflecting his dependence on electricity.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When the group invokes the optional Cold Equations rule in a high- or medium-plausibility game, the challenged player chooses before rolling: after a failure, aspect invocations may raise the result only to a tie; alternatively, each invocation gives only +1 instead of +2.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Plausibilometer — Optional Rule: The Cold Equations (fate-srd#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ordinary Fate resolution; turn on either stricter option when scientific consequences should constrain heroic flexibility, at the cost of making success harder.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A game’s big issue can be treated as an aspect and, when useful, as a setting element with aspects, skills, stunts, stress, and consequences. Changing the issue itself normally requires a significant or major milestone, reached by addressing specific problems or opponents.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Creating a Fate Space Game — Issues and Aspects — Big Issues (fate-srd#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to big issues as aspects; add fuller character-like statistics when broad, epic-scale change should be playable, at the cost of greater rules and tracking.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A previously backgrounded science-fiction detail can be brought into play as an aspect, and complications can then be added to it as situation aspects. Keep the total number of active setting aspects, including big issues and opened-up black boxes, to two to four.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Creating a Fate Space Game — Issues and Aspects — Setting Aspects as “Black Boxes” (fate-srd#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to leaving most technology as background; open it up when its consequences create useful trouble or opportunity, while limiting active setting aspects to two to four.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In a personal-tone game, the GM may make character aspects more important than situation aspects, including requiring at least as many character-aspect invocations as situation-aspect invocations for an action. In an epic-tone game, the GM may instead emphasize setting and situation aspects, and use the Bronze Rule or scale rules to enable larger-scale action.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Creating a Fate Space Game — Defining the Setting — Scope — Tone (fate-srd#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a balanced mix; shift aspect emphasis toward characters for intimate stories or toward situations and large entities for consequential, broad-scale play.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Coach Wimbly can implant a suggestion in a target’s mind only if he has used his mind-control app on them; the target can resist with Courage against Good (+3) passive opposition, even when alone.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Coach H. Wimbly — Stunts (fate-srd#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring prior app exposure and a Courage defense; a world could lower or remove that barrier to make the app more coercive, at the cost of reducing a target’s agency.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When an artifact with a higher tech level is used against a more primitive artifact, it creates an advantage with one free invocation per scene, or two if the tech-level gap is at least three. Tech level also sets the difficulty to overcome defenses at that level, and can set minimum effect on a successful attack or overcome or maximum effect on a successful defense; a defense ceiling normally wins unless the attacker succeeds with style.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Extras > High Technology > Tech Level (fate-srd#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated invocation and effect limits; a world can widen or narrow tech-level gaps, with sophistication explaining the advantage.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A power source can be treated as a pool of fate points that can be spent to invoke aspects concerning the devices it powers. A Cold Fusion Cell has refresh 2, and its output can be manipulated with Lore to create advantages.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Extras > High Technology > Tool Classes; Extra: Cold Fusion Cell (fate-srd#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a two-point cell pool; a world can change its refresh or require a skill roll, with limited stored energy as the constraint.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Astrogation sets a course by overcoming a difficulty based on route complexity and ship capability: a straightforward trip may be Mediocre (+0) or Average (+1), while a difficult generation-ship approach may be Great (+4), Superb (+5), or Fantastic (+6). Success with style can create a useful boost or shorten travel by one time shift; failure can mean no viable course, extra resource use, damage, or one or two additional time shifts.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Create New Skills > Astrogation (fate-srd#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a course roll with consequences chosen from the listed outcomes; a world can make navigation more or less hazardous, with time, fuel, or ship damage at stake.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A Near-Future EVA Suit protects its wearer from vacuum for several hours at Good (+3) duration, provides Fair (+2) zero-gravity mobility through thrusters, and has an Average (+1) voice-only communicator.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Extras > High Technology > Extra: Near-Future EVA Suit (fate-srd#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed duration and ratings; a world can make suits last longer or provide more functions, with equipment sophistication setting the limits.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Telempathic Healing can reduce another person’s consequence by one severity step once per session after an Empathy roll against Mediocre (+0) for mild, Fair (+2) for moderate, or Great (+4) for severe. On success the healer takes a mild consequence; on failure the healer can still succeed at a cost by taking a consequence at the severity healed.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stunts > Empathy > Telempathic Healing (fate-srd#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-step healing once per session with the stated difficulty and personal consequence; a world can ease or tighten the cost, with the healer absorbing the strain.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Camouflage Circuit lets its user spend a fate point to leave the scene and later return at a place they could have reached unseen, even interrupting another action. If the user did not act in the exchange of departure, they may act immediately on return; otherwise they act in the next exchange.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stunts > Stealth > Camouflage Circuit (fate-srd#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fate-point cost and reachable-location limit; a world can restrict when or where reentry is possible, with visibility and timing balancing the escape.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: On a node map, travel is possible between locations connected by a path, and paths may be treated as equal or assigned different travel time or effort. Unconnected systems are beyond the typical ship’s range or endurance; on a zone map, movement within a zone is trivial while crossing between zones takes effort.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Spacecraft and Space Travel > The Space Map (fate-srd#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to connected routes and trivial within-zone movement; a world can vary path costs or add connections, with distance and ship endurance limiting travel.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Psychic powers generally create advantages by affecting the world, such as clouding a target’s mind, evoking a fear, or disrupting equipment; the target resists with the specified skill. A Psychic Blast stunt permits a Psionics attack resisted by Will or Psionics.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Create New Skills > Psionics; Stunts > Psionics > Psychic Blast (fate-srd#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to advantage creation resisted by the target, with attacks available only through the stunt; a world can broaden psychic uses, with resistance and access to the skill as limits.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: On maps that encode adjacency, movement between nonadjacent locations requires crossing intermediate locations, although a route can directly link far-apart zones. An open map imposes no movement grid: with suitable transport, characters can go anywhere shown, and travel time follows real-world constraints and vehicle capabilities.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Open Map (fate-srd#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to adjacency-gated travel on zone or node maps; turn the dial to unrestricted destinations on open maps, with vehicle capability and travel time as the remaining limits.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A spacecraft’s available change in velocity depends on its thrust and fuel efficiency, and travel may be impossible if its delta-vee is insufficient. On a planetary launch, high thrust and high specific impulse are generally needed to reach orbit without boosters or other assistance, unless advanced technology removes that requirement.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): A Little Bit of Rocket Science (fate-srd#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring sufficient delta-vee for a journey; a setting can relax launch limits with advanced drives, at the cost of plausibility or specialized technology.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: For interplanetary trips, the travel-time chart ranges from several months to a few centuries for low-thrust, low-efficiency engines, and from a day to several months for high-thrust, high-efficiency engines, depending on distance category. If a travel-time roll succeeds with style, reduce the time by one step; success at a cost can add one or more steps or require extra fuel, while complete failure means the ship lacks the delta-vee to make the trip.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Interplanetary Travel (fate-srd#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the chart’s engine-and-distance travel times; a world can speed or slow journeys by changing engine capability, while failed planning can consume fuel or make a route unreachable.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Relativistic travel makes time pass more slowly aboard the moving ship than for observers at rest. At .90c, for example, a 100-light-year voyage takes about 50 years aboard but about 110 years at home; for game purposes, noticeable effects need not be applied until speeds exceed .5c.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Interstellar Travel at Relativistic Speeds (fate-srd#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ship-time and home-time diverging above .5c; a setting can ignore the effect or make it central, with lost time away from home as its cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: The Wang-Chaudary Vortex Drive needs enormous energy and is usually powered by antimatter; it is typically engaged at the outer edge of a star system after a months-long journey. Navigation or engineering errors can send a ship to a distant location in the past or future, while passengers undergo brief disembodied sensory deprivation, sometimes with hallucinations.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Example Hyperspace Drive: The Wang-Chaudary Vortex Drive (fate-srd#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring costly antimatter and a safe system-edge departure; turn the dial toward temporal accidents or sensory harm to make miscalculation more consequential.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A Millennium Drive ship can initiate a warp only if a confederation waystation is within a few light-years; the field interacts with the station’s warp field. Meeting another warp field sends both ships onto a new shared vector, so interception can slow or strand a target; travel difficulty begins at Average (+1) for distances above 5 and below about 55 light-years, then rises one step per tenfold increase.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Example Warp Drive: The Millennium Drive (fate-srd#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to beacon-limited warp travel and field interference; a setting can extend beacon reach or make interceptions more common, at the cost of less predictable routing.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Artificial wormhole stations hold a one-way route open using continuously powered negative-mass fluid; endpoints must be at least several light-years apart, with practical routes reaching perhaps a dozen light-years. The Autorité du Portail charges transit fees to fund upkeep and expansion of the network.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): A Wormhole Network (fate-srd#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-way, maintained portals with transit fees; a world can add return routes or longer links, but needs more rare fluid and ongoing power.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A human crew using the Millennium Drive must succeed at both an Engineering action to power up the drive and a Pilot action to reach the destination; Astrogation can create an advantage for either or both. Engineering failure can cause damage or control problems, while Pilot failure can cause delays, navigation errors, or hazards; the pilot has limited control because the ship rides a warp field.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Example Warp Drive: The Millennium Drive (fate-srd#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to separate drive-start and navigation checks with distinct failure consequences; a world can waive the checks for experienced crews, while experimental technology makes failures more likely.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A rapid or erratic hull-pressure drop can injure occupants, but the most urgent vacuum threat is oxygen loss: unconsciousness occurs in about 10 seconds and death after about a minute without oxygen. Microgravity weakness can be mitigated by exercise or equipment; maintaining the regimen requires an Athletics roll, with a few weeks at Average (+1), and a tie causes a mild consequence while failure causes a moderate or severe one.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Life in Space (fate-srd#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to timed oxygen loss and cumulative microgravity consequences; a world can soften them with suits, shielding, or artificial gravity, at the cost of protection and upkeep.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A ship can be represented by aspects that authorize characters to use ship-related skills; access to a fighter craft and a pilot aspect, for example, permits a dogfight attempt even with Pilot at Mediocre (+0) or lower.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): As a Setting Element or Aspect (fate-srd#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to aspects granting fictional permission; a setting can require stronger training or ship access, reflecting specialized technology.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When combining character and ship skills, the lower rating can impose a -1 modifier on the higher rating, while a higher rating can grant +1 to the lower; equal ratings have no effect. Alternatively, a character’s success can be followed by a separate effect roll using the ship’s skill, with +2 on that roll for success with style.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): As Skills (fate-srd#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single combined rating; turn on separate effect rolls when the gap between operator skill and equipment quality should matter, at the cost of slower resolution.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Ships may receive one to three free stunts and a refresh rating to buy more; taking a fourth stunt reduces refresh from 3 to 2. Ship-pool fate points may be spent by its captain to help any crew member’s action.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): As Stunts with Refresh (fate-srd#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three free ship stunts and refresh 3; a world can raise or lower the allowance to change how capable ships are, balanced by the refresh cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In standard movement, a ship moves one zone per exchange for free; an overcome action can move it farther, such as one extra zone at Mediocre (+0), then one more for every two shifts. A ship undertaking a special maneuver cannot evade enemy fire and defends with Mediocre (+0) Pilot.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Step 3: Establish Movement Rules — Standard Movement (fate-srd#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one free zone per exchange and skill-based extra movement; a setting can make special maneuvers easier or harder to emphasize agile or hazardous travel.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Under burn movement, changing zones requires spending delta-vee and succeeding at a Pilot burn to move one adjacent zone; failure can create danger or damage. Low fuel can be tracked as a minor resource cost or a major-cost aspect, and stronger gravity wells increase burn difficulty.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Step 3: Establish Movement Rules — Burn Movement (fate-srd#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one adjacent zone per successful burn; a world can make burns cheaper or more difficult according to available fuel and gravity, reflecting propulsion limits.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In range-zone combat, ships sharing a zone can use very short-range weapons, ships one or two zones apart can use beams, and ships three or four zones apart can use missiles or torpedoes; at seven or more zones apart, or off-map, a ship has broken off combat. Missiles resolve immediately within two zones, next exchange within four, and the second next exchange within six; torpedoes move by the gunner’s Shoot roll and attack on entering the target’s zone.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Range Zones (fate-srd#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these range bands and ordnance delays; a world can alter ranges and flight times to reflect its weapon technology.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A station has aspects, stunts, and battle stress; when harmed, it must take stress or the ship takes a consequence. Losing all station stress takes out both the station and its occupant, while a player may instead concede by losing the character or abandoning the station. A taken-out station cannot be used until restored.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Battlestations (fate-srd#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to station stress and shared ship consequences; a world can increase station durability or ease repairs to make crew roles more resilient.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: For each step of size difference, the larger ship gains +1 to attack or defense or both, plus Weapon rating 2, Armor rating 2, or both; the smaller craft may gain +1 per step on maneuver-related create-advantage or overcome actions against it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Differences of Scale (fate-srd#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one bonus step per size difference; a world can change the bonuses to make scale either decisive or more surmountable.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An engineer can spend a fate point and overcome with Crafts against difficulty equal to twice a taken-out station’s battle-stress boxes to restore it; it returns with one fewer stress box than before.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Battlestations — Engineer — I Don’t Know How Long She’ll Hold (fate-srd#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fate-point repair with a doubled-stress difficulty and reduced capacity; a world can ease repairs or restore more capacity, at the cost of weaker damage consequences.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A player can spend a fate point or a free invocation to make an aspect produce a defined mechanical effect beyond its ordinary use. The effect should be worth about two shifts of potency and do something specific rather than add a static bonus.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Invoking for Effect (fate-srd#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow paid aspect effects at roughly two shifts; tune their potency or availability to set how flexible aspects are, with fate points or free invocations as the cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A simple limit is one special effect attached to each player character’s high concept. More effects are possible, but keep each character to one or two at most; reserve them for important NPCs as appropriate.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): How Many Effects? (fate-srd#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one effect per player character and at most two per character; raise or lower the cap to adjust complexity, because too many choices can slow decisions and go unused.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character should normally have no more than one or two aspect effects; one or two may be free, while a GM can require refresh for additional effects.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Aspect effects (opening passage) (fate-srd#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one or two effects, turn the limit or refresh price to set character flexibility, and charge refresh to keep extra effects from becoming too common.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: With scaled invocations, a tenuous aspect grants only a reroll; a relevant one grants the usual +2 or reroll; a perfect one automatically succeeds, or on an attack sets effort to skill plus 3. A perfect non-attack success counts as 1 shift, and a relevant second aspect can add success with style.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Scaled Invocation (fate-srd#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ordinary invocation unless using these tiers; tune how strictly aspects must fit to change the power of spending fate points, with perfect fit as the price of automatic success.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character may destroy a usable situation aspect by explaining how it becomes unusable; if the group accepts the explanation, the character gets one free invocation, then the aspect is replaced by a new aspect representing an imminent, complicating danger.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Detonating Situation Aspects (fate-srd#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing detonation only when it creates a worse imminent situation; loosen or tighten acceptance to trade dramatic destruction against scene stability.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Under low-powered aspects, invoking multiple aspects on one roll can provide rerolls, but the +2 bonus can be chosen only once total for that roll. The Keen Senses stunt is an exception on Notice rolls, allowing any number of aspect invocations if the player can pay their fate-point costs.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Low-Powered Aspects (fate-srd#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one +2 maximum, with rerolls still available; grant the stunt exception to make perceptive characters stronger, at the cost of fate points.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A quest aspect is available to any PC in the group for invocation and can be compelled as though on every PC’s sheet, granting each a fate point. Resolving the quest counts as a milestone, scaled to its difficulty and duration.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Quest Aspects (fate-srd#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to shared access and group-wide compel rewards; narrow who can invoke or receive points to make shared goals less influential.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Conditions can absorb stress: checking a fleeting condition reduces stress by 1, a sticky one by 2, or a lasting one by 4, and multiple conditions may be checked for one hit. Fleeting conditions clear after a chance to recover, sticky ones need a specific event, and lasting ones need at least one session plus Great (+4) passive opposition to begin recovery; their two boxes clear across recovery and another full session.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Conditions (fate-srd#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated 14 total stress absorption and recovery timings; adjust condition types or their absorption to control endurance, with lasting conditions imposing time and treatment.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Modes set the starting rating of every included skill; a skill shared by two modes improves one step, and one shared by all three improves two steps. Players then receive 7 points for improvements, with no skill rising above specialized.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ratings; Reinforced Skills; Improving Skills (fate-srd#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three modes rated Good (+3), Fair (+2), and Average (+1), with the 7-point improvement budget; alter mode overlap or points to change breadth and specialization.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A triggered stunt requires its stated narrative condition and skill roll, then grants its specified effect on success; ties should bring a lesser benefit at a cost, and failures can bring suitable repercussions.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Triggered Effects (fate-srd#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to success-only full benefits, with a costly partial result on ties; adjust failure consequences to set how risky powerful conditional stunts feel.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A stunt normally costs one refresh, with three free stunts and three refresh as the stated baseline; a stunt combining two stunts’ benefits, such as a 4-shift effect, costs two refresh. Stunt costs can instead be paid in other ways, such as fate points, stress, an action, or an enemy boost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stunt Costs; Combined Stunts (fate-srd#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the baseline refresh cost, raise or lower it to tune stunt access, and use alternative activation costs when the in-world benefit should carry an immediate burden.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A race supplies one or two aspects and a racial skill, which can be assigned to an empty skill slot. The skill’s listed uses and chosen flavor determine its applications; each additional flavor costs one stunt or one refresh.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Race: Elf / Race: Orc (fate-srd#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one flavor; a world can permit more by charging a stunt or refresh, representing the effort or flexibility required.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states
