rules.statement: During an origin story, a player who would otherwise roll a skill at Mediocre (+0) may put that skill in an empty slot instead. When the player accepts or invents a suggested aspect in a moment of trouble, they may invoke it once for free and gain a fate point.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Origin Story — Choosing New Skills / Choosing New Aspects (fate-srd#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to learning skills and aspects through play; a world can vary how often these opportunities arise, trading structured character growth for faster or slower development.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A GM may offer a fate point to use a PC aspect as an adventure seed. If the player refuses, they do not lose a fate point; the GM should choose another aspect instead. Suggestions can be made into situation or adventure aspects, and good suggestions can earn fate points.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Pre-Compels as Adventure Design (fate-srd#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a voluntary offer with no penalty for refusal; a world can make adventure hooks more or less compulsory, changing player control in exchange for the story’s direction.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An aspect event has a sequence of three to six aspects followed by a crescendo aspect. Introduce them in order as the story advances; they can be invoked or compelled while relevant, and reaching the crescendo signals that events have become especially dire.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Aspect Events (fate-srd#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to introducing the next event when the story has a lull; a world can speed up or slow down the sequence, reflecting how quickly threats escalate.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In a chase track, the fleeing side tries to empty a stress track and pursuers try to fill it. On a failed roll the opponent chooses a hostile boost or moves the track one check their way; a tie lets the roller move it one check their way but gives the opponent +1 on their next roll; success moves it one check, while success with style moves it two or one plus a boost. A track of 10 is a baseline, 14 is a major scene, and 18–20 may occupy a session; starting around 5 of 10 is typical, while 7 of 10 makes escape harder.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Special Circumstances — Chases (fate-srd#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 10-box track starting halfway; a world can lengthen the track or start it nearer full to make the chase longer or escape less likely.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An NPC’s motivation guides an instinct. Characters can use social skills to discover the motivation, change it, or persuade the NPC that another instinct better serves it; attempts usually face active opposition, and a contest or conflict may fit more involved situations.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Special Circumstances — Social Conflict — Motivations and Instincts (fate-srd#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to changing an instinct before replacing a motivation; a world can make beliefs more or less resistant, reflecting how deeply the NPC is committed.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: For each scale step separating two entities in conflict, the larger may gain +1 to attack or defense, or deal +2 shifts of harm or reduce incoming harm by 2. These benefits apply only when scale differs.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Customized Tools — Scale (fate-srd#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one listed benefit per scale step; a world can make scale gaps matter more or less, representing differences in size, reach, resources, or influence.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Characters can voluntarily check a stress box for a roll bonus equal to that box’s value. Alternatively, they can voluntarily take a consequence for a bonus of +2 for mild, +4 for moderate, or +6 for severe; either choice can make results swingier and affect the fate-point economy.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Customized Tools — Stress / Consequences (fate-srd#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to no voluntary harm-for-bonus option; a world can allow it for larger bonuses, at the cost of stress capacity or lasting consequences.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A failed action can still succeed by checking a Wealth stress box to pay a real monetary cost, such as overpaying or acquiring needed gear. PCs begin with 2 Wealth boxes, plus 1 per wealth-related aspect to a maximum of 3; checked boxes clear only when a parcel of Wealth has enough value to cover them, and adding boxes is allowed only at a milestone by replacing an aspect.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Starting Wealth / Gaining Wealth (fate-srd#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 2 boxes, with aspects raising the cap to 3; a setting can make wealth scarcer or more abundant, reflecting how difficult it is to recover from costly successes.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A weapon rating sets minimum stress shifts on a hit: Weapon 3 deals at least 3 shifts, but higher rolled damage stands. Armor sets maximum shifts taken, from rating 4 for light armor down to 1 for the heaviest; armor overrides weapons, except a success with style ignores armor.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Damage Floors and Ceilings (fate-srd#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to weapon minimums and armor caps; a world can turn lethality up with stronger weapons or down with stronger armor, trading swift injury for longer fights.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: On a successful attack, a weapon aspect can be invoked for a Fate point to make the target take a consequence instead of stress: light causes mild, standard moderate, and heavy severe. Success with style raises severity by one; the target may accept the offered point or refuse it by paying one of their own, in which case they take normal stress instead.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Armor and Weapon Aspects (fate-srd#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to consequence-forcing weapon invocations at the listed severity; a world can limit heavy weapons or alter the Fate-point exchange to make severe injury rarer or more costly.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Armor aspects can absorb consequences without filling the matching consequence slot: light absorbs one mild, medium one moderate, and heavy one severe or two mild/moderate. Exceeding the armor’s capacity breaks its aspect, requiring repair that may take hours to days and may cost something.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Armor and Weapon Aspects (fate-srd#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed absorption capacities; a world can make armor more durable or fragile, with repair time and expense determining the cost of exceeding its protection.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: With colored dice, each point of Red replaces one Fate die on an attack; on a tie or better, each Red die showing plus adds 1 harm shift. Each point of Blue replaces one die on defense; on a failure or tie, each Blue plus absorbs 1 harm shift. No roll can include more than 4 Red or Blue dice.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Red and Blue Dice (fate-srd#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to up to 4 substituted dice; a world can increase or decrease weapon and armor colors to make harm more or less variable.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A minor supplemental action creates one boost lasting until the actor’s next turn begins. An opponent may use it against the actor or their action, removing it; the GM may also compel it once for free, after which it disappears.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Supplemental Actions (fate-srd#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one short-lived boost per minor action; a world can expand or restrict eligible actions, balancing tactical flexibility against the risk of being hindered.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Stormcalling requires an aspect naming an attuned storm and costs 1 Refresh if weapon/armor ratings are used, otherwise 2. Its effects must project and shape storm force externally; attacks have no range penalty in-zone and take −1 per zone of distance, while barriers normally span zones and have a rating equal to the caller’s roll, with rolls below +1 producing no substantial barrier.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stormcallers — Mechanics / The Stormcaller Skill / Barriers (fate-srd#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to external, storm-themed effects and the stated Refresh and range costs; a world can restrict available storms or increase their costs to keep magic from eclipsing mundane characters.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Storm-specific rules modify the shared actions: Earthquake and Glacier gain +1 when creating barriers; Flood barriers lose 1 rating per exchange unless maintained at a −1 penalty to later actions; Inferno barriers lose 2 per exchange under the same maintenance cost; Thunder barriers vanish after 1 exchange unless maintained at that cost. Other storm rules can alter attacks, defenses, or movement, including Glacier freezing a target with a movement barrier equal to half damage rounded up.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stormcallers — Earthquake / Flood / Glacier / Inferno / Thunder (fate-srd#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the element-specific modifiers and barrier decay rates; a world can change duration or maintenance penalties, making powerful barriers easier to sustain or more fleeting.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character chooses two blessings from their Vizier without spending more refresh; being chosen has already cost 1 refresh. After great service aligned with the Vizier, the character may take another related aspect, spend 1 more refresh, and choose two additional blessings.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The blessings themselves; Advancement (fate-srd#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two blessings for a 1-refresh mark; a world can grant more for further refresh costs, reflecting deeper service to a Vizier.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A curse or blessing normally takes about half an hour, ritual trappings, and a successful Average-difficulty roll against one person or an object up to house-size; it lasts three days and nights, or a week on success with style. An absent target raises difficulty by +1 with a strong symbolic link, +2 with an unclear link, or +3 if only named; a small group under twelve or a large site adds +3, and only one spell can affect a target at once, with a new one replacing the old.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Subtle Art — Mechanics (fate-srd#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary, subtle aspects and one spell per target; a world can increase reach or duration, at the cost of stronger rituals or less uncertainty.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A spell’s area effect is a scene aspect usable by anyone there. A secondary subject can raise difficulty if absent, but a token accepted by that subject counts as presence and must be used within three days.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Subtle Art — Mechanics (fate-srd#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a shared scene aspect rather than a private effect; a world can make spells target-specific, requiring access to the subject or a timely token.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Conjuration summons an elemental using a circle and a sacrifice, with difficulty set by its type. Failure still summons it but leaves it free, a tie gets one service of less than a night, success binds it for a week, and success with style binds it for a month; the summoner can dismiss it nearby, and a successful renewal lasts a week or a month with style.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Storm Summoners — Skill: Conjuration (fate-srd#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a week-long service bond and a sacrifice; a world can extend service with stronger rolls, risking an uncontrolled creature on failure.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A Conjuror’s skill limits both the number of bound elementals and their combined summoning difficulties. On renewal failure a creature is released; a tie lets its bond expire normally. A circle improves defense against summoned creatures by +1 to +4 depending on its construction.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Storm Summoners — Skill: Conjuration (fate-srd#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a capacity budget equal to the skill rating and circles that strengthen defense; a world can raise capacity, making simultaneous bindings easier but harder to manage.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A Storm bargain costs 1 refresh, restricts the character to that Storm, and creates an aspect the patron can compel; breaking the bargain removes its benefits and turns bound creatures against the character. The replacement Summoning skill permits patron-element creatures without sacrifices, makes failed summons flee, and treats skill as 4 higher for binding capacity.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Storm Summoners — Elemental Bargains; Skill: Summoning (fate-srd#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-refresh bargain with obligations and restricted element; a world can offer greater power for more bargains, risking patron conflict and loss of control.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A named elemental summoned through a bargain is Superb, has 4 stress boxes and -2/-4/-6 consequences, and gains its Storm’s listed bonus. In elemental combat, the strongest creature sets attack and defense at +1, while non-Wisp allies add +1 to suitable advantages or overcome actions.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Storm Summoners — Skill: Summoning; Elementals in Combat (fate-srd#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one powerful named creature with combat support from other elementals; a world can allow more simultaneous allies, increasing bookkeeping and the exposure of the summoner’s bindings.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Magic has no direct attack or defense use in its basic form; it creates blessings or curses as aspects, normally through ritual, and its apparent effects remain within plausible outcomes. If made overt, the spell list can include concrete supernatural effects and durations can rise to a lunar month.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Subtle Art — Magic and Reality; Variations and Options (fate-srd#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to subtle, short-lived effects that can be mistaken for coincidence; a world can make magic perceptible and concrete, extending effects to a lunar month.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A wizard’s duel uses Magic instead of Fight and inflicts mental damage until one wizard is taken out; the victor may decide whether the defeated wizard dies. A greater being drawn into such a duel may survive defeat but carry a consequence forward.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Subtle Art — Wizards’ Duels (fate-srd#032)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a mental contest with potentially lethal consequences; a world can make duels less dangerous by forbidding death, or more costly by carrying consequences forward.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A summoning uses one Lore roll against both the creature’s summoning difficulty and the text’s parsing difficulty; both targets are hidden from the player. If the roll beats the summoning target but not the parsing target, the summon works but the GM gains Doom Points equal to the shortfall, with a tie counting as a one-point shortfall; failing both can mean failure or an unprotected creature loose.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Summoning (fate-srd#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a low summoning target and a harder, source-dependent parsing target; raise parsing difficulty when reliable instructions are scarce, making research and imperfect safeguards the price.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A stylish success on a ritual produces no Doom Points and lowers that character’s parsing difficulty for that same ritual by 1 on later attempts, but never below the summoning difficulty; other users retain the original difficulty.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Summoning (fate-srd#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-point personal improvement after an especially good result; a world can make shared notes more useful, reducing the cost of learning rituals.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A summoned creature is bound and cannot act freely until its summoner releases some or all of it; release can permit a creature to use its abilities under agreed limits. Doom Points can let it exceed those limits, call other creatures, contact a prospective bargainer, or impose a scene aspect whose radius grows over time.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Binding; Doom Points (fate-srd#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to creatures being contained until deliberately released; turn up the danger by letting accumulated Doom erode restrictions, at the cost of escalating complications.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Channeling first creates a Summoned Power advantage, then a spell roll uses Mediocre (+0) plus its accrued bonuses; casting difficulty depends on the spell. A result below Average causes mental stress equal to the gap from 0, while casting in one action requires an aspect invocation without its +2 bonus or a suitable stunt.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Limits — Channeling (fate-srd#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to preparing power before casting and risking mental stress on a poor result; allow fast-casting stunts to reduce the preparation cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In the optional burnout rule, a caster may take a consequence during the spell roll and add a bonus equal to the stress that consequence would normally prevent. In the alternative channeling-risk rule, the caster declares Fair (+2) through Epic (+7) as the target, takes stress equal to any shortfall, and uses that declared level as the spell roll if successful.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Limits — Channeling (fate-srd#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to power bought with bodily or mental harm; a setting can make the exchange more generous or harsher by changing the consequence bonus or declaration range.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Fated Mana converts each point of lost refresh into 1 mana point (MP), or 2–3 MP if the conversion rate is adjusted; MP refresh like fate points but can only fuel magic. Suitable magical aspects can generate MP instead of fate points when invoked under the system’s ritual limitations.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Fated Mana Points (fate-srd#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one MP per lost refresh and restrict MP to magic; increase the rate when magic should be more readily available, balanced by limiting its uses.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: For blood magic, each point of physical stress taken generates 1 MP, and each suitable bloody consequence generates MP equal to its shift value; the stored MP lasts until spent or until the injury is recovered.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Blood Magic (fate-srd#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting injury into temporary magical fuel; adjust the yield or duration to make bodily harm a more or less attractive price.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A power item takes a day of work in an appropriate environment and a moderate cost to create, plus a Great (+4) roll; success stores 1 MP and success with style stores 2. A user may maintain as many such items as their magic skill’s numeric value, while a replenishing item takes a month and great cost and is limited to one per user.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Borrowed Power — Items of Power (fate-srd#033)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to small, stealable stores of one or two MP with a skill-based capacity; increase craft time or cost when portable magical reserves should be rarer.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Arrow moves the user by line-of-sight teleportation up to about 100 feet (3–4 zones) per jump, but only along a route the body could physically traverse; it stops before obstacles. Each jump costs 1 MP, and the enhanced version costs 2 MP to reach any clearly visible distance.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Arrow; Tweaks (fate-srd#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 100-foot, physically traversable line-of-sight jump for 1 MP; a world can extend range to any visible distance for 2 MP because extra reach consumes more power.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: After taking physical damage, the user can spend MP retroactively to gain armor equal to the MP spent. If a blow is known in advance, spending 3 MP instead prevents all damage for a heartbeat.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ironskin (fate-srd#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to armor paid for after harm, or total brief protection for 3 MP; a world can vary the timing or price because the defense is short-lived.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Pomp costs 1 MP to let the user converse with a physically intact corpse. Its enhanced form costs 3 MP to animate a body in suitable condition for a scene; it follows basic instructions.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Pomp; Tweaks (fate-srd#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to conversation for 1 MP; a world can allow temporary animation for 3 MP because moving a body is more demanding than speaking through it.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Rider costs 1 MP to enter the mind of a visible mammal, ride its senses for about two minutes, and leave its thoughts and actions inaccessible. Each additional two-minute period costs 1 MP, and another visible target can be reached for an additional MP; while riding, the user’s body is helpless. The enhanced version costs 3 MP per jump and makes the user’s body disappear, returning behind the last subject.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Rider; Tweaks (fate-srd#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sensory riding with the body left helpless for 1 MP per two minutes; a world can enable bodily disappearance for 3 MP per jump because it adds a major relocation effect.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Sight gives an erratic warning when supernatural activity is present; spending 1 MP reveals details. Its enhanced use costs 1 MP to learn one hidden fact about a person or thing, once per target, without guaranteeing the desired information.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Sight; Tweaks (fate-srd#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an unreliable warning and paid details; a world can allow one paid hidden fact per target because information is uncertain and limited.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Terror costs 1 MP to create a scene-long aura; the user may choose physical or mental stress when attacking, and self-preserving animals avoid the zone. For another MP, eye contact and a successful intimidation create a target’s Fear of the user aspect, freely invokable by the user for the rest of the scene; spending 2 MP total instead intensifies the aura so attacks also inflict mental damage equal to physical damage.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Terror; Tweaks (fate-srd#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a scene-long fear aura for 1 MP, with extra MP buying a target aspect or intensified damage; a world can adjust duration and potency to set how costly fear is.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When short of MP, a character may underline an aspect to gain the missing amount; that aspect becomes tainted and no longer grants fate points when compelled, instead granting 1 MP. The taint can also produce dark compulsions.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Power use and tainted aspects (fate-srd#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to filling an MP shortfall by tainting an aspect and replacing its compel reward with 1 MP; a world can change the amount or consequences because the power puts the character’s soul at risk.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character with a cyber-heart must tie an aspect to being a cyborg and reduce refresh by 1. The heart powers other augs, filters blood impurities and toxins, and lets its user spend a fate point to ignore poison or toxin, or to concede rather than be taken out by a lethal event it could plausibly avert.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Cyberware — Cyber-Heart (fate-srd#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a cyborg aspect and 1 refresh for the heart; a world can tune its fate-point protections because installed enhancements carry both a power source and an agency cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A gadget’s stunts cost 1 refresh each, and it has a function aspect and a flaw aspect without using the character’s personal aspect slots. Each additional flaw can reduce its refresh cost by 1, but a gadget with stunts costs at least 1 refresh.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Gadgets and Gear — Functions and Flaws; Stunts; Additional Flaws (fate-srd#034)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one function and flaw aspect plus 1 refresh per stunt, with added flaws discounting cost to a 1-refresh minimum; a world can set how severe flaws must be because drawbacks balance reliable benefits.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A player gives up their personal action to rally the squad for a squad-skill roll or stunt. Each additional squadmate who gives up their next action to help lowers the task’s difficulty by 1; the roll’s result applies across the unit, and squad-wide stress is dealt equally to each squadmate.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Squad-Based Action — Rolling Squad Skills (fate-srd#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one rallying player and shared results; a world can make extra helpers lower difficulty more or less, reflecting how effectively the unit coordinates.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A mass-combat unit may move one unobstructed zone for free and take one action. A leader can spend their action to give it a second action, or a player can spend a fate point to do so for a unit without a leader; a unit cannot repeat an action in the same turn, and an attack ends its turn.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): THIS MEANS WAR: MASS COMBAT — Unit Actions (fate-srd#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one action plus a free move; a world can make extra actions easier or harder to obtain, reflecting leaders’ coordination or the cost of spending fate points.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A unit that puts Pinned Down on an enemy prevents it from moving zones unless it first succeeds at an overcome action opposed by the attacker’s Shoot. The aspect ends if the target successfully moves or the attacker does not spend an action to maintain it on a later turn.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): THIS MEANS WAR: MASS COMBAT — Create an Advantage (fate-srd#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring ongoing action to sustain the restraint; a world can change how long suppression lasts, reflecting the attacker’s attention and ammunition.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In a two-person physical duel, only the combatant holding the upper hand can make an attack. A combatant gains it by succeeding with style using a non-harm skill, but must take it instead of the action’s usual success-with-style reward; a successful style roll for turn order can also grant it at the start.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): SWASHBUCKLING DUELS (fate-srd#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a transferable advantage earned through non-attack skills; a world can make it harder or easier to claim, reflecting how tactical or theatrical duels are.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A superskill can be activated by spending a fate point to double its current skill bonus for one roll. After the roll, reduce the skill by one step; it refreshes next scene if it has not fallen to zero, but an exhausted skill needs rest or recharging before it can be used again.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): SUPERS — Super Skills (fate-srd#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-step fatigue per use and scene-based recovery; a world can adjust the cost or recovery interval, reflecting how taxing superhuman effort is.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In a contest between superpowered characters, either may spend fate points to oppose, cancel, or raise an action, with bidding continuing until one declines. A tie sends all bids to the GM; a clear winner receives the losing side’s bids.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): SUPERS — Creating Super-Powered Stunts (fate-srd#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to open-ended bidding with the loser’s points transferred; a world can cap bids or alter the payout, reflecting the desired volatility of its fate-point economy.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A vehicle can have at most 5 aspects; a Crafts overcome roll to customize it has a baseline difficulty of 0, increased by 2 per existing aspect, and can add or feasibly remove an aspect on success. Vehicles have no stress: one with 3 or fewer aspects can take one mild consequence, while one with 4–5 can take one mild and one moderate; a suitable aspect may permit a severe consequence.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): VEHICLES — Custom Cars; Vehicle Damage (fate-srd#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the five-aspect cap and consequence limits; a world can raise or lower durability and customization difficulty, reflecting the vehicle’s robustness and complexity.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A medium never rolls merely to enter the otherworld; access is assumed, and each ritual stunt provides a channeling or projection method usable once per session.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Frontier Spirit — Stunts: Ritual (fate-srd#035)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reliable access once per session through a chosen ritual; a world can make access less reliable or more frequent, reflecting how difficult or familiar the otherworld is.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A ritual stunt can be used once per session and requires both a deliberate, distinct ceremony and an unusual precondition that the practitioner must seek out or prepare. Channeling reaches only one spirit-facet per ritual and requires being in that spirit’s territory; projection lets participants explore the otherworld more deeply and may cause permanent harm.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ritual stunts (fate-srd#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one use per session, with a prepared ritual and special circumstance; a world can relax either limit, at the cost of making contact less exceptional or more dangerous.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character may have at most one stunt for exceptional high technology. Such a stunt grants permanent access and reliable ownership, but high technology cannot self-reproduce or self-repair, create matter or food, provide portable real-time global communications, or teleport people or objects.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): High Technology (fate-srd#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one reliable advanced device per character and the listed capability bans; a world can loosen the bans, at the cost of undermining scarcity, communication limits, or travel challenges.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: During an immanence episode, connected characters perceive and remember the otherworld clearly. Important unconnected characters perceive it but need a successful Will roll to distinguish it from mundane reality; failure causes a catastrophic misreading, and their memories later become vague. Supporting and nameless NPCs have progressively less reliable perception and memory, and are highly vulnerable to spirits.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Immanence (fate-srd#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to clear perception for the connected and confusion or vulnerability for others; a world can make unconnected people more perceptive, reducing the otherworld’s secrecy but also its threat.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Facets that share portfolio aspects eventually share experiences, memories, and knowledge, though the transfer may be delayed or unclear. Greater facets treat lesser facets’ isolated experiences as unrepresentative, while lesser facets regard greater facets’ experiences as authoritative.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Facet Aspects (fate-srd#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to imperfect, gradual information-sharing among related facets; a world can make it faster or clearer, at the cost of making secrecy between facets harder.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A facet taken out in physical conflict is not killed: it is bound and banished until the next major milestone, then returns shaped by the views of facets sharing its portfolio. A supporting or main facet can instead take an extreme consequence that separates it from its parent and leaves it out only until the scene ends; the renegade becomes erratic and must be mediated separately.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Facet Stress and Consequences (fate-srd#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary banishment for ordinary defeat and a risky, destabilizing separation for an extreme consequence; a world can make defeat permanent, at the cost of removing spirits as recurring actors.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A facet’s Dream Invasion works on someone near things representing all its portfolio aspects during the previous day; the target can detect it with Notice or Empathy, and an aware target can end it by winning a Will contest. Poltergeist lets a facet act on objects for one fate point per exchange while all its portfolio aspects are represented in the scene; it ends if any required aspect is removed. Chain of Coincidence builds toward a change over several hours, using Rapport for helpful effects or Provoke for harmful ones.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Manifestation Stunts (fate-srd#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to circumstance-bound manifestations with explicit detection, cost, or duration limits; a world can broaden access or reduce costs, making spirit interference more frequent and harder to resist.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Whenever a god spends a fate point to affect an action roll, move the intention token one step toward the approach used. Tokens begin one step toward each ascendant approach; pushing a token off its track transforms the god into a monster, while token positions at milestones determine the milestone tier.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Intention (fate-srd#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to intention moving with every fate-point expenditure and monsterhood at the track’s edge; a world can change the movement rate or threshold, trading slower transformation for less pressure on the god’s identity.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A god’s stations are a marked sub-region and a community; stored power there delays monster transformation and fuels mantle boons. A tier 1 boon may provide a persistent minor benefit and a stunt that spends one stored power point for +1 to a chosen approach and action in a stated circumstance; a geas imposes a -1 penalty in circumstances opposed to the god’s nature.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Stations; Boons; Geasa (fate-srd#036)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two sacred stations, where stored power supports boons and postpones transformation; a world can allow more stations or cheaper boons, at the cost of weakening the connection between place, power, and restraint.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A geas either penalizes actions contrary to a god’s nature by an amount equal to the current tier, or bars an action until the scene has enough enabling aspects—one per tier. At tier 0, the geas has no effect.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Geasa (fate-srd#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a tier-scaled penalty or aspect gate; a world can choose a harsher cost, because divine identity constrains conduct.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Gods and their monster forms cannot normally be killed, even when taken out; they can instead be imprisoned or otherwise prevented from acting, and can return later. During a twilight of the gods, this protection ends and they can be slain or permanently confined.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Also, You’re Immortal / …Except When You’re Not (fate-srd#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to eventual return after defeat; a twilight can remove that safeguard, making death a lasting world change.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When a fate-point expenditure would push an intention token off its track, the god must store the excess, bleed it into the surroundings, or become a monster. A god can also choose to become a monster at any time with an ascendant approach at tier 3.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Intention and Power / Becoming a Monster (fate-srd#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to offering storage or environmental fallout before loss of control; a world can make voluntary transformation available at tier 3, at the cost of control.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Each station can hold 1 power point. When a token would move toward a higher tier, its owner can store 1 point instead; points can be spent on boons, vanish between tales, and are lost if their station is lost. A god can also fill an empty station at any time by spending a fate point.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Storing Intention / Losing Stations (fate-srd#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one stored point per station, usable as boon fuel; a world can alter station availability, which controls the god’s reserve.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A god can bleed off intention just before a token would move in either direction, leaving it still and making the GM worsen or create a local refinement aspect. The result reflects the god and the intention; bleeding multiple steps makes the change more intense or widespread.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Bleeding Off Intention (fate-srd#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an unwanted local change in exchange for avoiding a token shift; a world can widen its reach, with broader and harsher fallout.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: At tier 1 or higher, a god can spend 1 power point to add a bonus equal to their tier to a suitably concept-related roll. At tier 2, power points can also be spent like fate points while invoking an ascendant aspect, without changing intention; at tier 3, a point can make a concept-related event happen.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Boons (fate-srd#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concept-bound, tier-scaled benefits bought with stored points; a world can widen what counts as concept-related, increasing the scope of divine effects.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A monster’s transformation immediately removes player control, but the player determines how the current scene ends. The monster can change the local landscape, and anyone it attacks must accept defeat or flee with an immediate consequence.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Becoming a Monster (fate-srd#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single catastrophic scene-ending outburst followed by GM control; a world can broaden its effects, at the cost of surrendering the character.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Bleeding off all accumulated intention at a tale’s end resets tokens to their starting positions. Fallout scales with total movement: 1–2 steps cause ordinary local harm, 3–4 produce hostile refinement, 5–6 affect a larger or multiple areas and create hatred toward the god, and 7 or more create numerous hostile sub-regions across similar terrain types.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Destroying the Status Quo (fate-srd#037)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fallout proportional to the number of steps erased; a world can amplify the geographic reach, making avoidance of personal power gain dangerous to many places.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A ship without size stunts is small: it carries 20 guns, 100 crew, and up to 300 tons of cargo. Each size step over another ship gives the larger ship +1 to attack and defend against it.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ships as Characters (fate-srd#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated capacities and size-based combat edge; a setting can change the scale of ships, with larger hulls requiring more crew and cargo capacity.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A character directly commanding a crew task substitutes their own skill for the crew’s, must participate, and cannot command another task at the same time; only one character can command a given task.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ship Skills; Crew Actions (fate-srd#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one active command per character and task; a world can permit delegation more freely, at the cost of less direct player influence.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In ship combat, each ship may perform each of four activities—maneuvers, repairs, gunnery, and signaling—once per exchange, and they may happen simultaneously. A ship can send one message per exchange, at roughly 40 words per minute; normally signaling takes the sender’s action but needs no roll.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ship Combat — Running the Conflict (fate-srd#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one use of each activity per exchange and the stated message rate; a world can speed or restrict communication, changing how quickly crews coordinate.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A ram requires first creating a position aspect that targets the enemy; while it remains, the attacker can use Sail to attack, and then must defend its own ship against that same attack. Failure damages the attacker normally.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ship Combat — Maneuvers (fate-srd#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the two-stage approach and risk of self-damage; a world can make ramming safer or more dangerous by changing the self-defense outcome.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Ship damage can be absorbed with consequences, crew conditions, or both. Bruised and Battered clear after rest and wound care; Light Losses and Heavy Losses persist until crew replacements arrive, and each represents one-tenth and one-quarter of maximum crew respectively.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ship Consequences and Conditions (fate-srd#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed casualty fractions and recovery limits; a world can make crew replacement easier or harder, affecting how long losses constrain a ship.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A ship sailing with fewer than three-tenths of its full crew cannot defend competently and is immediately taken out if combat begins. Missing crew must otherwise be represented by Light Losses and Heavy Losses conditions.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Ship Consequences and Conditions (fate-srd#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the three-tenths minimum; a world can lower or raise the threshold, with undercrewed ships becoming more or less viable in battle.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A conspiracy has three hidden campaign aspects—its alliance, goal, and weakness. The first time the GM invokes each one, or when players uncover it, that aspect is revealed and thereafter the players may invoke it normally.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Conspiracies — Conspiracy Aspects (fate-srd#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to keeping these aspects secret until invocation or discovery; a world can reveal them earlier, trading mystery for clearer leads.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A conspiracy’s approaches form a pyramid with three at Good (+3), two at Great (+4), and one at Superb (+5). They set passive opposition to efforts against its work; the GM may spend a fate point to substitute one for an NPC or mook’s usual roll bonus, replacing the whole mob bonus, including teamwork.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Conspiracies — Using Conspiracy Approaches (fate-srd#038)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated ratings and fate-point cost for substitution; a world can change the pyramid or payment, making conspiracies more or less formidable.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A standard special effect is available when a power succeeds with style or its user spends a fate point; an improved effect follows the same trigger but requires a separate stunt purchase.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Special Effects / Improved Special Effects (fate-srd#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing an effect only on those triggers; a world can make improved effects easier to buy or use, at the cost of reduced rarity or power.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A drawback is an aspect attached to a power’s user and does not replace the character’s trouble. Choose one listed drawback or invent one.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Drawbacks (fate-srd#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one drawback aspect per power; a world can increase or waive drawbacks, trading complications for less constrained powers.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A collateral effect can be used at any time, but doing so adds a situation aspect to the surrounding area; the GM decides what that damage looks like each time. A character may choose an effect from a power they lack, or devise one based on that power.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Collateral Damage Effects / Other Collateral Damage Options (fate-srd#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing flexible collateral effects with an area aspect as their price; a world can narrow the options or raise the price to limit versatility.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A summoned creature is created once per scene with one aspect, one Good (+3) skill, two physical and two mental stress boxes, and mild and moderate consequence capacity; it leaves or dissipates at scene end, clearing consequences. In a conflict it acts on its controller’s turn; both may move freely, but only one may act.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Creature Summoning (fate-srd#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one controlled creature per scene with a fixed modest stat package; a world can expand the stable or improve its stats, at the cost of added power.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A duplicate created once per scene can appear up to one zone away, shares its creator’s aspects and skills but takes −1 on rolls, and has its own physical stress capacity; mental stress it takes is suffered by its creator. It may be dismissed, otherwise fading at scene end; during conflict both move but only one acts.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Duplication (fate-srd#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one short-lived, weakened copy with shared mental injury; a world can permit more or stronger copies, at the cost of control or safety.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A summoned item is limited to one at a time and lasts a few minutes or until scene end, though its user can dismiss it sooner. A hand-held, simple object faces Average (+1) opposition; larger or more complex objects raise that opposition, and each additional item summoned in the scene raises it by +2.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Item Summoning (fate-srd#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary simple objects with rising difficulty for size, complexity, and repeated use; a world can relax those limits, at the cost of resource scarcity.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Influence uses Rapport to attack against Will. Nameless targets who are affected must attempt a short-term task until it succeeds or the scene ends; named characters and player characters may obey or take mental stress. Orders cannot require direct self-harm or an inevitably fatal act.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Influence (fate-srd#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to short, non-suicidal orders with a meaningful choice for named targets; a world can strengthen control, at the cost of consent and autonomy.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When energy absorption successfully defends against an energy attack or overcomes an energy obstacle, its enhanced version grants one boost reflecting the absorbed energy; only one such boost may be held at once.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Energy Absorption (fate-srd#039)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to storing a single brief boost from successful absorption; a world can allow more stored energy or longer retention, at the cost of balance and possible overload.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A power that creates a boost or field may limit how many can be active, how far they reach, and how long they last; for example, basic amplification allows one boost at a time, within touch, and the boost expires at scene end if unused.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Power Amplification — Basic Power Amplification (fate-srd#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one touch-delivered boost lasting until use or scene end; increase its range or capacity only by granting an enhancement, with stronger output potentially causing collateral harm.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A nullification field increases opposition to opposed power uses by +2; powers without opposition instead require overcoming a Fair (+2) Will obstacle. The user is unaffected and may dismiss the field, while enhancements can increase opposition or extend the field.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Power Nullification — Basic Power Nullification (fate-srd#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a user-safe zone field with +2 opposition or a Fair (+2) obstacle; broaden or strengthen it at the cost of concentration, fatigue, or misfires.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Power replication requires touch and may be resisted; it grants only one stunt’s worth of a target’s power at a time, without special or collateral effects. A lingering copy ends at scene end or when another power is copied; full-suite copying takes several minutes and lasts a scenario, but replaces the copier’s own powers meanwhile.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Power Replication — Basic Power Replication and Enhancements (fate-srd#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a resisted, touch-based copy of one limited effect; allow broader copying for longer setup and temporary loss of the user’s own abilities.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A slowing effect targets one person up to one zone away and prevents movement between zones until released or overcome against the creator’s roll. A zone-wide version takes a −2 penalty and affects everyone there, allies included; complete entanglement also takes −2 and prevents physical actions until escape.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Slowing — Basic Slowing and Enhancements (fate-srd#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single target restrained from changing zones; expanding to a zone or stopping all physical actions also affects allies or imposes a −2 penalty.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A shield can separate the user’s zone from an adjacent one until scene end or dismissal; matter cannot pass through. The user defends against attacks on or through it with Will, choosing to take the shifts as mental stress or let the barrier break and take half the shifts, rounded down; each extra barrier after the first reduces defense by one.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Shielding — Basic Shielding (fate-srd#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a scene-long, opaque-to-matter barrier between neighboring zones, with defense paid for in mental stress; maintaining multiple barriers weakens defense.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Weather created in the user’s zone lasts until dismissed, the user leaves, or scene end. Its difficulty is generally Fair (+2), rising for extreme or seasonally unlikely conditions; an enhancement can let it persist from an adjacent zone.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Weather Control — Basic Weather Control (fate-srd#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a scene-limited weather effect in the user’s zone at Fair (+2) difficulty; make extremes harder and allow persistence or wider reach through enhancements.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Basic shape-shifting can take the form of any creature after a Will-based advantage attempt, usually against Fair (+2) opposition, with unusually large, small, or complex forms harder to achieve. The form lasts until ended or the user is taken out.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Shape-Shifting — Basic Shape-Shifting (fate-srd#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a creature form lasting until dismissal or incapacitation, with Fair (+2) opposition; restrict forms or raise difficulty for a world with tighter transformation limits.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A telepath may read minds within the same or an adjacent zone using one chosen skill; a target who knows or suspects the intrusion may oppose with Will. The user can also project words to minds in range.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Telepathy — Basic Telepathy (fate-srd#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to nearby mind-reading limited by the selected skill, with active resistance once detected; broaden range or grant deeper access only as an added capability.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Teleportation moves the user up to three zones as an action if the destination is visible. A marked location can instead be recalled from any distance, but only one location may be marked at a time.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Teleportation — Basic Teleportation and Mark and Recall (fate-srd#040)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a visible-destination jump of up to three zones; permit unlimited-distance recall only to one prepared mark, which can be changed.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A corruption effect can wither virtually everything in your zone; living targets resist more and take only 2 physical stress, while inanimate things such as walls and floors crumble to dust.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Corruption — Collateral Damage Effects (fate-srd#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to decay affecting the whole zone, with living targets limited to 2 stress; a world can narrow the affected area or increase resistance because living things withstand the effect.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A dramatic mutation can be triggered once per scene by spending a fate point, switching the ranks of two skills that are next to each other in rank.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Corruption — Enhancements (fate-srd#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one adjacent-rank skill swap per scene for a fate point; a world can change the frequency or price because the mutation is a costly burst of adaptation.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An electrical user can briefly become electricity and pass through conductive material as an action, including a barrier connected to a metal doorknob. A user can also travel between city outlets, but must know roughly where the destination outlet is and overload electronics there.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Electricity Projection — Enhancements; Collateral Damage Effects (fate-srd#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to conductive passage as an action and outlet travel with destination knowledge and equipment damage; a world can restrict routes or reduce the overload cost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A fire user can direct flames by overcoming a Fair (+2) obstacle with Provoke; more complicated maneuvers raise the opposition. An effect that surrounds the user in fire lasts until scene end, but can be ended voluntarily; touching the user inflicts a mild physical consequence or 1 stress if no consequence slot is open.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Fire Projection — Enhancements; Collateral Damage Effects (fate-srd#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Fair (+2) opposition for simple flame direction and scene-long burning with a voluntary end; a world can raise difficulty or shorten duration because complex control and sustained flames are harder.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: An ice slick fills the user’s zone or an adjacent zone, is easy for the user to cross, and presents a Fair (+2) obstacle to others until the user’s next turn. An ice shell grants Armor:4 against the next attack, but movement or a physical action ends it sooner.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Frost Projection — Enhancements; Improved Special Effects (fate-srd#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-turn slick and a single-attack Armor:4 shell; a world can widen or extend either effect, balanced by how long the terrain or protection persists.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A Roar aspect is created against a base difficulty of +2. While it lasts, its creator may use only the approach used to create it and the two approaches connected to that approach; it ends when the creator uses a non-adjacent approach or at scene end.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Advanced Conflict — Roar Phase; Losing Your Roar Aspect (fate-srd#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a +2 creation difficulty and a three-approach limit until scene end or a forbidden approach; a world can loosen the restriction because the heightened state costs flexibility.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Failing to create a Roar aspect still creates it, but gives the GM a related consequence to use against the character; on a tie, the GM gets a boost instead. A minor NPC unable to take consequences simply fails rather than gaining an aspect at this cost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Advanced Conflict — Creating a Roar Aspect (fate-srd#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an aspect plus a GM consequence on failure, or a boost on a tie; a world can make the risk milder or harsher because ambition invites backlash.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In a zone, a side with at least twice the opposing weight may change one of its rolled dice to [+] on a relevant roll; at four times the target’s weight, an attacker may change two dice. Apply changed weights from the next roll after the sides’ totals shift.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Advanced Conflict — Weight in Combat (fate-srd#041)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one die at 2:1 and two at 4:1, recalculated on the next roll; a world can adjust thresholds because superior numbers or size provide leverage.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: In social contests, weight measures authority and influence rather than headcount: at court a monarch weighs 8, a high-ranking Houselord 4, a small-house Houselord 2, and commoners 1 regardless of number; in scholarly debate, a renowned academician weighs 4, an ordinary professor 2, a graduate student 1, and commoners 0 until enough gather to total 1.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Example Weights (fate-srd#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to status-based weight; a world can turn weight up or down for rank and credibility, because those decide whose voice carries influence.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Weight-0 creatures cannot affect a creature of weight 1 or more unless numerous; defeating one individually uses overcome rather than conflict. A human-sized swarm weighs 1, a bear-sized one 2, and a troll-sized one 4; multiple huge swarms can occupy separate zones and cooperate. While outweighing opponents, swarms ignore ordinary attacks that do not affect an entire zone and cannot be moved by opposed movement; a wide-area effect or aspect invoked for effect can make an attack affect them.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Swarms (fate-srd#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to swarm size as weight and zone-scale resistance; a world can tune swarm size or area-attack access, with broad effects needed to harm or shift a mass.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Moving to an adjacent, uncontested zone is free. Obstructed or longer movement requires overcome and costs the turn's action; passive obstacle difficulty is +2 if either zone has an adverse aspect and +4 if both do, with +2 per extra zone and +2 per adverse aspect along the route. A blocker creates active opposed opposition, which can invoke adverse terrain for +2 each; overcome always permits success at a serious cost.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Movement on the Battlefield (fate-srd#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to free adjacent movement unless opposed or obstructed; a world can raise route difficulties or costs, because terrain and blockers impede travel.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A successful opposed overcome can push an opponent one zone, or pull them along one zone. Charging into adjacent melee doubles the attacker's weight for that attack; success with style also pushes the foe one zone in a straight line, while failure gives the foe a boost in addition to normal failure consequences. Full Defense grants one free invocation against each attack that turn, ending when the defender takes another action; Full Attack requires overcoming Good (+2), makes the next attack lethal on success, and gives the opponent a boost for their next attack.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Maneuvers as Actions (fate-srd#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these declared action maneuvers and their tradeoffs; a world can alter their reach or risks, with exposed attackers paying for greater damage.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A melee attack with a heavy weapon that succeeds with style can knock its target back one zone; any melee attack succeeding with style can disarm, disabling associated equipment stunts until an overcome at +2 retrieves a weapon or shield, or move the attacker one zone despite opposition. These replace the usual boost and are used immediately.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Maneuvers as Boosts (fate-srd#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these immediate effects on stylish melee success; a world can limit them by weapon or circumstance, since they trade away the usual boost.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Lethal attacks bypass stress and go directly to consequences; a successful lethal attack inflicts lasting trauma, or instantly defeats minions without consequences. They can come from a maneuver, a relevant stunt, a battle ritual, a naturally deadly creature, or exceptionally favorable attack conditions judged by the GM; stunt access is once per session and ritual access once per conflict.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Lethal Attacks (fate-srd#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to lethal attacks bypassing stress; a world can narrow eligible sources or frequency, because the result causes lasting injury or immediate minion defeat.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Casting a ritual requires an appropriate permission-granting aspect and an overcome roll; a successful general ritual creates a temporary stunt on one target, while a battle ritual is cast before conflict at Fair (+2) and creates a situation aspect with free invocation for the priest's side. General rituals usually start at Average (+1), with difficulty increased by distance, absent symbolic links, target size, unwillingness, divine displeasure, and other complications. One target can have only one ritual at a time; a new one replaces the old. Ritual casting adds a group Divine Interest consequence unless done as a three-part challenge to evade notice, cast, and conceal the act.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Magic: The 30-Second Version; Casting A Ritual; Battle Rituals (fate-srd#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary ritual effects and the listed target modifiers; a world can make casting more discreet or harder, balancing magic against divine attention.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: The group tracks four Divine Interest consequences: two mild, one moderate, and one severe. Listed triggers include certain extreme dice results, results of +9 or better or -4 or worse, rituals, specified magical-stunt costs, and substituting divine attention for a personal consequence. Mild consequences clear at a minor milestone; moderate ones last at least two sessions and until a significant milestone, when they can be reduced to mild; severe ones last through at least one significant milestone and until the next major milestone. Filling all four and gaining another takes the group out; at session end it receives a Divine milestone, clears the consequences, and agrees on a new group aspect.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Divine Interest (fate-srd#042)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to accumulating shared divine attention with milestone-based recovery; a world can change triggers or recovery pace, while overreach risks divine intervention and group defeat.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Ancient devices are generally represented with aspects; a useful device that grants a practical benefit can also have a stunt, while a frequently used or damageable one may have a stress track and a minor consequence. A working device’s stunt may grant a bonus or a special effect, and its uses can be limited; when all use boxes are checked, the stunt permanently stops working.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Mechanics; Creating Wonders: The 30-Second Version (fate-srd#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to aspects for most wonders, add a stunt for practical effects, and limit uses or add stress when scarcity or wear should matter; the setting’s lost knowledge and fragile devices justify those costs.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A discovered wonder can have one to three less-obvious aspects when it matters to the adventure; reveal a hidden aspect through play and use only as many aspects as needed. A working ancient apothecary, for example, grants +2 to recovery checks for illness, and its use can be limited to a particular illness or exhausted supplies, even after one use.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Mechanics; Example 1: An Ancient lighthouse; Example 2: The ruins of an Ancient apothecary shop (fate-srd#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a small number of discoverable aspects and a narrowly useful stunt; widen the scope or uses if the wonder is meant to transform the story, while scarce ancient supplies provide an in-world limit.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Once restored and when climate conditions permit, an ancient canal and lock system can move a ship between two bodies of water at different elevations once per session, twice a day, or another GM-chosen reasonable interval.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Mechanics; Example 3: The ruins of an Ancient canal and lock system (fate-srd#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one ship passage per session; the GM can change the interval, while damage, lack of water, or ice can prevent operation.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A functioning ancient compass grants +2 to Carefully overcoming obstacles when orienting a course. A multi-tool can instead provide one or two free invocations of its high-concept aspect per session; ordinary invocation for it still costs a fate point.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Mechanics; Example 4: Ancient compass; Example 5: Ancient multi-tool (fate-srd#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a narrow navigation bonus or a small allotment of free multi-tool invocations; damage and the item’s limited usefulness can constrain its benefits.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: Adventure opposition has Combat, Exploration, Interaction, and Lore ratings: set one to the PCs’ highest approach plus 1, two to that rating minus 1, and the remaining one three lower. These ratings oppose PCs through NPCs or environmental obstacles; the selected highest and lowest ratings steer the adventure toward harder and easier kinds of action.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Opposition; Adventure Stats (fate-srd#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated rating spread and assign ratings to the intended themes; shift which approach is hardest or easiest to shape the adventure’s challenges and risk of Divine Interest.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A minion gets +2 for tasks it is skilled at, −2 for tasks it is bad at, and +0 otherwise, with zero to two stress boxes and no consequences; once its stress is gone, the next hit takes it out. A group adds one stress box per two members to an individual’s usual stress and combines members’ physical weights, splitting the group if its total weight exceeds 8.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Opposition; Characters and Creatures; Groups of Minions (a.k.a. Mobs) (fate-srd#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to simple skill categories and low stress for disposable opposition; increase group durability by adding members, but split groups beyond weight 8.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: A swarm’s size sets its weight: small is weight 1, big weight 2, and huge weight 4. Small swarms have no stress boxes, big swarms one, and huge swarms two or three.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): The Opposition; Characters and Creatures; Swarms (fate-srd#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the size-based weight and stress values; the GM can raise size and staying power to make a swarm a more substantial threat.
rules.licence: CC-BY-3.0/4.0 or OGL as each book states

rules.statement: When an adventure approach applies, use its rating as the difficulty; otherwise, a trivial task is +0 or can succeed without a roll, a tough task is +2, an extremely difficult one is +4, and an impossible task can be set higher. In tense situations, a difficulty may be two above the approach used, and a fitting or problematic approach can shift the target by 1 or 2.
locators: Fate SRD (Core, Condensed, Accelerated, toolkits): Setting Difficulties (fate-srd#043)
rules.speaker: rulebook
